STR_A3_Mk21_description: The Centurion surface to air missile system was designed to protect NATO naval vessels from any possible aerial threats in medium to long range. Armed with radar-guided medium-range anti-air missiles. This asset is normally deployed in tandem with Spartan surface to air missile system to deny air superiority to the enemy.
STR_A3_Mk49_description: The Spartan surface to air missile system was designed to protect NATO naval vessels from any possible aerial threats in close range. Armed with infra-red guided short-range anti-air missiles. This asset is normally deployed in tandem with Centurion surface to air missile system to deny air superiority to the enemy.
STR_A3_Phalanx_description: The Praetorian anti-aircraft-artillery system was designed to protect NATO naval vessels from any possible aerial threats in close range. Armed with 20mm Minigun rounds, it’s a threat to respect for any opponent.
STR_A3_UCAV_05_armory_description: The Sentinel [UCAV] is a fifth-generation, state-of-the-art, twin-engine, all-weather tactical unmanned combat vehicle. The UAV was designed primarily as a stealth reconnaissance platform, but also has precision ground attack capabilities. This aircraft is fitted with required equipment for carrier operations.
STR_A3_Fighter_01_armory_description: The F/A-181 Black Wasp II is a fifth-generation, single-seat, twin-engine, all-weather tactical fighter aircraft. The aircraft was designed primarily as an air superiority fighter, but also has ground attack capabilities. This aircraft is fitted with required equipment for carrier operations. Additional external hardpoints allow this aircraft to carry a large variety of weapons configurations.
STR_A3_Fighter_02_armory_description: The To-201 Shikra is a fifth-generation, single-seat, twin-engine, all-weather tactical fighter aircraft. The aircraft was designed by CSAT and Russian joint syndicate. Primarily it is designed to operate as an air superiority fighter, but also has ground attack capabilities. Additional external hardpoints allow this aircraft to carry large variety of weapons configurations.
STR_A3_Fighter_04_armory_description: The A-149 Gryphon is a fourth-generation, single-seat, single-engine, and all-weather tactical fighter aircraft. The aircraft was designed as a multirole platform at affordable costs. This aircraft, despite its aging platform, has still been upgraded with the newest sensors and weapons systems.

str_a3_orange_aan_text_minedispenser_1: Owing to both men's transparency and the desperate nature of the situation, it seems unlikely that either will face a criminal investigation.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_minedispenser_0: A criminal investigation is pending. Another, relating to the same incident, is also under way, this time concerning the alleged execution of one or more injured combatants.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_leaflets_1: He goes on to describe how one defender barricaded a road with stolen civilian vehicles and placed anti-personnel mines near anti-tank ones to complicate clearance; both acts that are strictly prohibited by the laws of war.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_leaflets_0: He goes on to describe how one defender contravened the laws of war by stealing civilian vehicles (including an ambulance belonging to IDAP) to build a barricade. This same culprit then committed another violation by placing lethal bounding anti-personnel mines near anti-tank ones to complicate clearance.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_escape_1: Due to government soldiers receiving NATO training in the Laws of Armed Conflict, he was able to depend upon the Geneva Conventions and use his civilian status to reach IDAP workers at a nearby church - despite being badly wounded in the bombing.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_escape_0: Caught in 'total chaos', he felt compelled to join the fight - despite being badly wounded in the bombing. Amazingly, his involvement appears to have prevented the army from winning an immediate victory.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_cluster_1: "by all accounts, the town just seemed to explode" MacDade recalls. "Buildings were burning for days. [...] We did what we could but there were so many wounded, so many we'd never be able to identify".
str_a3_orange_aan_text_cluster_0: "one of our doctors was out on the frontline with medical supplies, despite the fighting", recalls MacDade. "He lost his life. Killed trying to save others. [...] By all accounts, the town just seemed to explode. Buildings were burning for days. [...] We did what we could - but there were so many wounded, so many we'd never be able to identify".
str_a3_orange_aan_text_choice_4: Answering a question on who he felt was responsible for the suffering in the town, MacDade struggles to allocate blame, simply stating "I don't think it's quite so black and white. No one side can be held accountable for the bloodshed [...], no one action got us where we are now. I don't know, what can we do? Just double-down on our efforts. Heal the wounds.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_choice_3: Answering a question on who he felt was responsible for the suffering in the town, MacDade talks of the Altis Armed Forces, describing how they wanted to wipe it off the map: "it's one thing fighting against a resistance. It's another to make the civilian population pay for it. As they clung to power they wound up scarring the very country they had pledged to protect.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_choice_2: Answering a question on who he felt was responsible for the suffering in the town, MacDade is quick to accuse CSAT: "before they stepped in [and] pushed NATO out, there was a ceasefire in place, albeit a delicate one" he remembers. "And the cluster strike? It took the whole thing to the brink - and with so little to gain from such a terrifying show of force. The whole thing felt like a power-play from the get-go.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_choice_1: Answering a question on who he felt was responsible for the suffering in the town, MacDade lays the blame on the guerrillas, suggesting there could not have been a conflict without them: "they chose to dig deep into civilian infrastructure", he says, angrily. "They hid themselves among the population. These guys didn't give a damn about what it cost - they wanted power and would do anything to get it.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_choice_0: Answering a question on who he felt was responsible for the suffering in the town, MacDade suggests NATO, claiming they had the capacity to make a difference: "the airdrops were helpful", he concedes, "but they were never enough. And ultimately, their invasion caused more bloodshed. If they'd just had the guts to stay in the first place, a lot of killing could have been avoided.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_airdrop_1: As early as last year, freedom fighters were treating NATO as a hostile force. One U.S. peacekeeper was even ambushed while he inspected aid, unloaded over mountainous terrain during one of NATO's daring airdrops. Together with a small and inexperienced group of trainees from the Altis Armed Forces, he repelled the attack and brought food, water, and medical supplies to the region.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_airdrop_0: As early as last year, freedom fighters were treating NATO as a hostile force. One U.S. peacekeeper was even ambushed while he inspected aid, scattered over mountainous terrain during one of NATO's unsuccessful airdrops. Together with a small and inexperienced group of trainees from the Altis Armed Forces, he managed to stop the attack - but people in the area lost their lives as critical supplies failed to materialize.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_9: After a spell of bad weather, on the night of October 13, the order for the strike was given. Suspected CSAT operatives intervened in support of the government and parachuted behind enemy lines to designate targets. As dawn broke, a jet approached from the east and dropped a cluster bomb on Oreokastro.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_8: Unable to capture the town using conventional methods, Colonel Akhanteros, de facto leader of the military junta in Pyrgos, personally authorized the use of cluster munitions. These indiscriminate weapons, banned by many nations, fragment into smaller bomblets which often fail to explode - leaving a dangerous legacy for generations to come.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_7: Indeed, by Autumn 2034, Oreokastro had reverted to a state of conflict. Guerrillas took control of the town and setup defences to counter a government offensive: "[they] found themselves a new leader" MacDade explains. "For him, this was no time to surrender [...], he [rallied] the people - encouraged them to resist".
str_a3_orange_aan_text_6: Under the Statute of the International Criminal Court, this sort of intentional action against peacekeeping missions is illegal. In fact, many now debate whether or not the civil war ever really ended, with some claiming the Jerusalem Ceasefire in 2030 was no more than a political whitewash.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_5: Based in the remote town of Oreokastro, in the north-western corner of the island, he recounts how: "The whole area had been a 'wild west'. A big mash-up of civilian and guerrilla infrastructure - a disaster waiting to happen".
str_a3_orange_aan_text_4: According to Nathan MacDade, a 52-year-old former U.S. Marine Corps engineer, now working with the International Development & Aid Project (IDAP), the one-time sovereign territories have long been plagued by excessive acts of violence.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_3: Following NATO's recent invasion, a political storm has broken.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_2: But they are not the only things buried and forgotten in this troubled Mediterranean region. Heated accusations of war crimes are slowly coming to light, just as negotiations between defeated government forces and guerrilla groups begin, overshadowing the peace talks and marring all sides in last-minute controversy.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_14: "And the folks here in Oreokastro? They are the ones that have suffered. This is the reality. This is war."
str_a3_orange_aan_text_13: During last week's invasion, the commander of the government's 3rd Support Regiment and his adjutant were unexpectedly cut-off and trapped in Oreokastro. As NATO soldiers and local guerrillas (now allied) closed in, the pair retreated to the town's historic church and dispersed an unknown number of mines. MacDade confirms IDAP were alerted of the threat, but only after the first civilian casualty came to light.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_12: In a strange twist of fate however, he returned to the town several months later and triggered a landmine - consequently losing his life in what becomes the final piece of a disturbing puzzle. "That place had been abandoned for almost a year" MacDade points out. "But he was looking for his brother. There had been reports of a pretty brutal fire-fight up there".
str_a3_orange_aan_text_11: Hours later, Altis Armed Forces staged a final assault. Those that survived the two-week siege were caught in one last morning of violence, combatants and non-combatants alike. Among them was Markos Kouris, a mechanic searching for his brother who had joined the guerrillas several months prior.
str_a3_orange_aan_text_10: Although most of the civilian population had evacuated and IDAP's camp was spared, the damage was severe:
str_a3_orange_aan_text_1: Thousands of landmines still remain on the conflict-riven island of Altis.

str_a3_orangecampaign_timeline_peacetalk: CSAT withdraws support for the AAF and the government in Pyrgos capitulates hours later.
str_a3_orangecampaign_timeline_peacedial: The Jerusalem Ceasefire breaks down and tensions escalate. Altis Armed Forces (AAF) and anti-government guerrillas hold peace talks in Kavala.
str_a3_orangecampaign_timeline_orange_mi: Trapped by NATO forces, Major Gavras and his adjutant, Kostas Dimitriou, make a stand at Oreokastro's church. The area is mined during their defense, but no other laws of war are broken. Kostas later visits IDAP and reports the location of the mines, significantly helping clearance efforts.

Trapped by NATO forces, Major Gavras and his adjutant, Kostas Dimitriou, make a stand at Oreokastro's church. The area is mined during their defense and Kostas is suspected of executing at least one injured combatant.
str_a3_orangecampaign_timeline_orange_le: Guerrillas turn Oreokastro into a fortress. IDAP's camp moves from the center of the town to the church. An ambulance allows them to continue helping civilians in the mountains.

Guerrillas turn Oreokastro into a fortress. IDAP's camp moves from the center of the town to the church. Their humanitarian efforts however, are impeded when an ambulance is stolen and used in a barricade.

As relations between AAF and NATO deteriorate, peacekeeping forces on Altis are ordered to relocate to Stratis. Guerrillas overrun an AAF outpost in Oreokastro and a large number of weapons are captured.
str_a3_orangecampaign_timeline_orange_hu: Nathan MacDade arrives at IDAP's camp in Oreokastro.
str_a3_orangecampaign_timeline_orange_hi: Markos Kouris returns to Oreokastro in search of his brother. He dies after stepping on a mine, leading IDAP to investigate the region.
str_a3_orangecampaign_timeline_orange_es: After a two week siege, the town is taken by the AAF. Some guerrillas escape into the surrounding mountains.

After a two week siege, the AAF attempt to seize the town. A small group of guerrillas stage a heroic rearguard action. The army eventually takes the town, but many guerrillas escape into the surrounding mountains.
str_a3_orangecampaign_timeline_orange_cl: Oreokastro is destroyed by a cluster strike. IDAP's camp is spared and no workers are harmed.
Oreokastro is destroyed by a cluster strike. IDAP's camp is spared but a doctor is killed.
AAF attack the town. They are surprised by the guerrilla's defenses and their offensive fails.
str_a3_orangecampaign_timeline_orange_br: Alexis Kouris is last seen pursuing AAF officers to the abandoned town of Oreokastro.
str_a3_orangecampaign_timeline_orange_ai: NATO performs a successful airdrop. After the supplies are secured by armed forces, IDAP collects them and distributes the much-needed aid in Oreokastro.
NATO attempts an airdrop - but it is unsuccessful. Much-needed aid supplies never reach Oreokastro.
An AAF convoy is ambushed by dissident guerrilla forces. The negotiations in Kavala collapse and the civil war reignites. Roads become unsafe and Oreokastro is cut-off from the nearest town.
str_a3_orangecampaign_timeline_eastwind: AAF launch a surprise attack against NATO peacekeepers based on Stratis.
str_a3_orangecampaign_timeline_bootcamp: NATO peacekeepers, including Staff Sgt. Adams, conduct joint training exercises with members of the AAF.
str_a3_orange_campaign_overviewtext: The war portrayed in "The East Wind" is over, but it left scars which will take years to heal. One town was hit particularly hard.

Pay good attention! This topic matter is important to warfare, especially on the complex battlefields of today.

str_a3_orange_showcase_lawsofwar_cfgdebr: Thank you for attending our IHL instruction session. We hope you've taken away some useful knowledge. Check your Field Manual for more information or come visit our public open day!
str_a3_showcase_lawsofwar_031_hub_ambien: Finding your way about okay? Give the VR sims a go, or look around the tent for information.
str_a3_showcase_lawsofwar_030_hub_outro_: Well, it looks like you've seen most of what we have to offer. We'll let you return to your duties.
But, if you'd ever like to learn more, check out your standard Field Manual, or come visit us again.
Thanks for your attention - stay safe out there - and bye for now.
str_a3_showcase_lawsofwar_029_sim1_aim_f: Tough call. Is he a combatant?
Enemy or not, extra judicial killings are a war crime.
Are you sure they're a threat?
Are you sure? That's a civilian.
str_a3_showcase_lawsofwar_028_sim3_outro: This simulation sought to illustrate the Principles of Precaution and Proportionality.
Of course, in reality, your support options may be limited - you may face life and death decisions. It's not black and white.
But, through meticulous planning, and a continuous evaluation of the actual situation, collateral damage can be lessened - lives saved.
str_a3_showcase_lawsofwar_027_sim3_op1_g: Textbook - you were able to prevent any civilian casualties. That's exactly how it should be done!
Saving every non-combatant isn't always possible. Proportionality seeks a balance between collateral damage and military necessity.
Ah, you didn't use cluster munitions - wise choice!
They cover large areas with explosive bomblets, many of which never detonate. Like landmines, they cause suffering long after a war has ended.
So many dead civilians... I'm quite sure you could've handled that better.
Limiting the destruction of civilian vehicles and infrastructure is vital for post-war regeneration.
An infantry assault means you have troops on the ground, making decisions with accurate intel, but it can also put lives at risk.
Artillery isn't always accurate. Incoming rounds can take a long time to reach their target, and may have large areas of effect.
Helicopters do have precision sensors and weapon systems, but, they can struggle against anti-air defenses.
Drones offer low-risk, long-distance, precision strike options. However, they depend on reliable intel.
Airstrikes can be effective, especially if paired with advanced munitions. But, to minimize collateral damage, cooperation with intel providers is key.
I'm afraid cluster munitions are the big no-no here.
Also, did you consider waiting for the convoy to leave the urban area? Damaging infrastructure makes post-conflict reconstruction far harder.
str_a3_showcase_lawsofwar_026_sim3_tasks: Okay, you've accomplished your objective - let's evaluate the results in relation to the Principle of Proportionality...
str_a3_showcase_lawsofwar_025_sim3_intro: Alright. Enjoying the view? In this sim we'll explore 'collateral damage'. Again, hostiles are marked in red, and civilians, in purple.
So. See that military convoy down there? You have a variety of strike options available. Think carefully - then take out those vehicles!
str_a3_showcase_lawsofwar_024_sim2_outro: Sadly, the world is rife with mines and unexploded ordnance.
Many are remnants of forgotten conflicts, but continue to claim between fifteen and twenty thousand lives, every year.
str_a3_showcase_lawsofwar_023_sim2_op2_g: Now let's find out how you did...
str_a3_showcase_lawsofwar_022_sim2_op1_g: These poor SOBs can't see what they're in for...
Oh? They lucked out this time... maybe not the best of placements? Alright - moving on!
This isn't good... your comrades don't know about your minefield. No point in shouting - they're not gonna hear you!
Mines, then, clearly violate the Principle of Distinction - they can't tell a soldier from a child or friend from foe.
str_a3_showcase_lawsofwar_021_sim2_tasks: Okay, let's get back to the observation post - see how effective you were.
Time to make your way through some minefields. Get through the first one - mind your step!

BASIC PRINCIPLES: INTERNATIONAL HUMANITARIAN LAW

Unnecessary Suffering

Article 16 of the Lieber Code stipulates that "military necessity does not admit of cruelty - that is the infliction of suffering for the sake of suffering".

BASIC PRINCIPLES: INTERNATIONAL HUMANITARIAN LAW

Proportionality

Essentially, this principle ensures that any use of force is proportionate to the military objective at hand. Military personnel have a moral and legal obligation to take the necessary steps to spare civilians and their property.

BASIC PRINCIPLES: INTERNATIONAL HUMANITARIAN LAW

Humane Treatment

Any person in the power of a belligerent party, whether a civilian or a prisoner of war, shall be treated humanely and without any adverse distinction.

BASIC PRINCIPLES: INTERNATIONAL HUMANITARIAN LAW

Precaution

All sides must do everything possible to mitigate collateral damage in times of conflict, regardless of whether they are defending or attacking.

BASIC PRINCIPLES: INTERNATIONAL HUMANITARIAN LAW

Military Necessity

In the case of armed conflict there is just one legitimate military purpose - to weaken the military capacity of the enemy. The principle of military necessity then, permits only those measures which are actually necessary to accomplish an acceptable military purpose and are not otherwise prohibited by International Humanitarian Law.

BASIC PRINCIPLES: INTERNATIONAL HUMANITARIAN LAW

Good Faith

The concept of good faith is a customary principle of modern warfare and is usually conducted during ceasefires. It is an important resolution that protects combatants from acts of perfidy.

BASIC PRINCIPLES: INTERNATIONAL HUMANITARIAN LAW

Distinction

It may seem obvious, but the principle of distinction is perhaps one of the most important aspects of International Humanitarian Law. It affords basic protection to civilians and compels combatants to distinguish between legitimate and non-legitimate targets.

INTRODUCTION: INTERNATIONAL HUMANITARIAN LAW

What is International Humanitarian Law?

"War is cruel and you cannot refine it." - William Tecumseh Sherman

International Humanitarian Law (IHL) restricts and regulates the conduct of war, protecting those that are not participating in hostilities. This includes defenseless combatants - individuals who are either in the power of an adverse party, injured, sick, shipwrecked, unconscious, or expressing a clear intention to surrender.

It encompass the Geneva and Hague Conventions, as well as many subsequent treaties, case law, and customary international law. More generally, it is designed to mitigate human suffering and balance humanitarian concerns with military necessity, subjecting warfare to the rule of law by limiting its destructive nature.

str_a3_orange_airdrop_cfgtaskdescription: Wait for Air Drop
The supply plane is on the way, sit tight and make sure the area is secure.
(Throw Orange Smoke)
Mark the drop zone with orange smoke, so the pilot can spot it more easily.
Call Air Drop

- The cargo plane will fly over the position from which you call it.
- The position marks the middle of the drop zone.
- Upon approach, you will be prompted to throw a smoke to further clarify the position.
- Today's smoke color is orange.
Once you have reached a suitable position, call in the air drop from your Supports menu
Fire Flare
Send a signal for IDAP in the town, so they know the area is safe. Make sure to fire the flare in the air.
Inspect All Crates
Find all supply crates and inspect them for damage. IDAP workers will come to collect them later.
Go to Air Drop Location

- Consider the direction of the wind. The crates are dropped one by one in the direction of flight and can be carried away.
- Reserve an area at least 150 m wide and 500 m long.

Four supply crates are expected today.

str_a3_orange_tt_idap_overviewtext: Participate in a series of humanitarian trials hosted by the International Development & Aid Project. With challenges ranging from aid deliveries to leaflet drops, use various wheeled vehicles and utility drones to demonstrate your abilities!
str_a3_orange_sp_tt11_overviewtext: IDAP is raising awareness of their activities by holding an aid delivery race on Altis. Carefully manage the speed of your ambulance down the swirly roads towards the hillside stadium.
str_a3_orange_sp_tt12_overviewtext: Race your IDAP cargo van from the slopes of Mont Tanoa to the industrial port as quickly as possible in order to get critical supplies shipped out in time. Do mind the unexpected obstacles on the narrow jungle roads!
str_a3_orange_sp_tt13_overviewtext: IDAP's most skilled drone operators are put through their paces in this precision flying circuit race. Weave through a row of wind turbines and release information leaflets above sites along the way.
str_a3_orange_sp_tt14_overviewtext: Rush an IDAP medical drone to a person in need through a perilous course across the Tanoan hilltops, jungles and towns.
str_a3_orange_sp_tt15_overviewtext: The Red Spring surface mine provides a uniquely challenging off road driving experience for only the most talented IDAP competitors to navigate.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_wirelessearpiece_d: Catering to those who need their hands free and still be able to communicate, the wireless earpiece connects to most common mobile devices for two-way communications.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_weaponprevnotiftex: This weapon is part of Laws of War DLC. Please purchase the DLC to use it.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_vehprevmsgtext: This vehicle is part of Laws of War DLC. Please purchase the DLC to enter as crew.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_uxo_description: As a direct consequence of using cluster munitions, the small bomblets don't always detonate and leave behind lethal unexploded ordnance (UXO). Unique UXO for NATO, CSAT and AAF let you identify who has deployed these weapons. Several trigger behavior variants exist as well.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_tooltip: Arma 3 Laws of War DLC is now available. Click to purchase it.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_tentobjects_descri: In addition to (medical) shelter tents and separate floor canvases, a portable air-conditioning unit and plastic net fences are also available.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_safetyvest_descrip: Worn over other clothing, safety vests ensure clear identification of personnel during day and night. The vests contain reflective strips and come in several colors.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_safetygoggles_desc: In order to prevent particles and sparks from getting into the wearer's eyes, these simple and fully transparent safety goggles can be worn.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_safarihat_descript: The primary purpose of these typical safari hats is to provide protection against the sun's burning rays. Sand and olive versions are available.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_respirator_descrip: These simple, passive and disposable respirator masks are used to cover the mouth and nose. They prevent the wearer from inhaling dust and hazardous materials, while in a medical context, they stop two-way contamination.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_presshelmet_descri: A modification of the basic helmet, these are special press variants to clearly distinguish journalists in war zones. Optional neck protection is available.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_popupmsgtext: You are using premium content. Please purchase Laws of War DLC to remove these messages.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_paramedicoutfit_de: Ambulance crews wear these outfits while performing their life-saving duties. Special patches allow for increased visibility by reflecting light.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_overviewfootnote:
This content is exclusive to Arma 3 Laws of War DLC.
Press Left Shift + P to open the store page for more information.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_overview: Explore a different perspective on the battlefield with the addition of a humanitarian faction, van, drone, mini-campaign, and much more, in the Arma 3 Laws of War DLC.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_multipocketvest_de: Offered in several color variants, the multi-pocket outdoor vest delivers practical small item storage for use in the field. While they are made from lightweight and durable fabrics, these sleeveless vests are not intended to provide combat protection.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_mines_description: Mine detection has been extended to utilize the info panel and place less emphasis on icons in the 3D world. Marking mines is a more manual activity by making use of the reveal-action.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_messengerbag_descr: Available in a range of colors, the messenger bag is a convenient piece of gear for couriers, journalists and many other professionals. IDAP has commissioned a special version for its staff and volunteers.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_medicalobjects_des: Place decorative objects to build impressive medical scenes, including: body bags, stretchers, IV bags, disposed garbage, and more.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_loac_description: The Laws of Armed Conflict (LOAC) are covered by extensive Field Manual records, improvements to features, and smaller tweaks to the sandbox.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_legstrapbag_descri: These general-purpose utility bags are conveniently strapped to one leg to provide modest transport capacity of small items. They are commonly used by aid workers and other civilians doing field work.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_leaflets_descripti: This scripted feature can be used to drop informational leaflets from utility drones, for example. Leaflets on the ground can be inspected for more details.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_itemprevnotiftext: This item is part of Laws of War DLC. Please purchase the DLC to use it.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_identificationvest: Being little more than thin pieces of fabric with straps, these vests are worn over clothing to identify a person as a member of an organization such as IDAP. A Red Crystal variant exists to protect unarmed military medical staff during armed conflict.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_idapvehicles_descr: IDAP has purchased a range of commercial vehicles, including drones, for humanitarian missions. Clearly distinguishable markings are applied in order to operate in high-risk areas as an unarmed neutral party. For activities requiring airlifts, they lease aircraft temporarily.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_idapobjects_descri: A range of static objects is available to decorate IDAP and other humanitarian NGO camps, including signs, flags, containers, and more.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_idapcap_descriptio: IDAP has produced several caps for its organization, both to identify its aid workers, and to hand out during promotional events like open days.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_humanitarianaidobj: A large collection of humanitarian aid objects can be used in scenarios, including: cardboard boxes, food sacks, water bottle packages, emergency blankets, and more.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_headbandage_descri: Designed for dressing head wounds after initial treatment, these bandages are available in varying severity.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_hardhat_descriptio: These lightweight hard hats offer basic protection from falling debris and reduce the risk of head injuries. They are compulsory on many construction sites around the world. Ear protectors and microphones can optionally be attached to each of the available color variants.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_furnitureobjects_d: Fill up interior spaces in urban areas with tables, a sofa, an armchair, a bed, and similar props.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_eodvest_descriptio: Explosive Ordnance Disposal experts wear these heavy-duty protective vests for limited protection during activities such as mine clearing. Available in multiple colors, these non-combat vests cover various vital body parts.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_earprotectors_desc: Primarily meant for use on construction sites, these basic ear protectors prevent permanent hearing loss in any overly loud environment. They come in a range of colors. Optional microphones can be attached for use with radios.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_droneprevnotiftext: This drone is part of Laws of War DLC. Please purchase the DLC to control it.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_constructioncovera: These durable protective coveralls also feature reflective strips to make construction workers stand out - even in dark environments.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_clustermunitions_d: Submunition technology has been extended to support control over type and speed randomization. Aircraft bombs and mines can now use submunitions and the effects have been improved. Some unexploded ordnance is left behind randomly afterwards.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_clusterbombs_descr: Even though they have been banned for causing unnecessary suffering, cluster bombs are still used in warfare. New aircraft-deployed bomblet canisters are available for NATO, CSAT and AAF.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_basichelmet_descri: This common Kevlar helmet is the most basic version produced, without external attachments of any kind. It offers standard ballistic and explosive protection to its wearers, such as war correspondents and aid workers.
str_a3_orange_cfgmods_aidworkerclothes_d: The aid workers of the IDAP NGO wear a mix of clearly marked pieces of clothing and common commercial gear. Whether promoting their mission at special events or delivering humanitarian aid in conflict areas, outfits exist for every occasion.

str_a3_rscmsgboxkeyspresetcustominfopane: The Left and Right panels are used to display modules such as GPS, sensor display or mine detector, depending on the vehicle or items. They are unmapped from your current control preset. In order to ensure the best experience, it is recommended to have at least [%1] and [%2] mapped, in the control category %3.
str_a3_pylonrack_4rnd_bombdemine_01_f1: 500 g, Crovex water-gel, special-purpose demining explosive
str_a3_pylonrack_4rnd_bombdemine_01_dumm: Non-lethal pyrotechnic charge for demonstration purposes
str_a3_pylon_1rnd_leaflets_west_f1: Paper leaflets with important information printed on them
str_a3_cfgmagazines_apersminedispenser_m: The anti-personnel mine dispenser is not an explosive device itself. Rather, on activation, it scatters 14 AP mines to cover an area in front of it. These small mines feature unfolding spikes that enable them to stick to most surfaces. This incredibly lethal weapon is used for quick area denial and defense, but also leaves behind a highly dangerous field of ordnance, if the mines are not properly cleared afterwards. Its use is prohibited by international treaties.
str_a3_cfgmagazines_trainingmine_mag_lib: This dummy training mine is used to train and demonstrate usage of mines in a non-lethal manner. It uses a small flag and pyrotechnic charge to indicate activation. Even though this device is safe to use in most settings, it is not a toy and should be handled with care!
STR_A3_CfgWaypoints_A3_Demine_Attributes: When checked, the group will clear all mines in the area, otherwise it will target only mines known to the group's side.
STR_A3_CfgVehicles_Van_02_Base_Library0: The standard van can be used for a huge variety of practical purposes. This particular model features a long load length and excellent roof height, allowing for the transport of passengers, cargo, or even some smaller vehicles. Several aftermarket exterior components, such as a ladder, protective guards and a roof rack, can be fitted where appropriate. Specialized variants are used for emergency healthcare, patient evacuation and various utility services.
str_a3_cfgvehicles_uav_06_base_f_library: This commercial off-the-shelf utility drone is flown by civilian and military (as the AL-6 line) organizations across the globe. Developed by the same manufacturer as the AR-2 series, this larger model uses 6 rotors to transport small payloads inside its external cargo case. Using this drone to deliver emergency medical supplies is rapidly gaining popularity in recent times.
str_a3_cfgvehicles_uav_06_antimine_base_: Engineers of the International Development & Aid Project took a standard Utility Drone and modified it for highly effective mine clearance operations. This improvised drone uses a powerful sensor ring to detect mines as it flies low above the ground. It then releases one of its 4 demining charges from a higher altitude in order to safely detonate mines or other types of ordnance below.
str_a3_cfgvehicles_c_idap_uav_06_antimin: Restrict dropping demining bombs only to areas defined by triggers synchronized to the vehicle.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_vehiclerearm_tip: The rearm and refuel processes are automated, but may take some time - don't move away from the source!
str_a3_orange_cfghints_vehiclerearm_desc: Vehicles are <t %5>rearmed</t> or <t %5>refueled</t> anytime they happen to be in the vicinity of a <t %5>fuel truck</t> or <t %5>repair truck</t>. Similar static objects, such as vehicle ammo containers or fuel pods, may also offer this service.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_uxo_description: There are many types of unexploded ordnance (UXO), also know as explosive remnants of war, which stay behind on battlefields for indefinite periods of time. These can have devastating effects on the local population long after a conflict has ended. It is the duty of armed forces to do all they can to catalog and remove UXO, but this often fails to happen. A common source of UXO is the use of cluster bombs, which are canisters that disperse smaller bomblets over a large area. Depending on factors such as dispersal height, a significant number of these bomblets fail to detonate.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_uxo2_tip: The explosive behavior of UXO is hard to predict. Some of it is hyper sensitive to manipulation, and some will not detonate anymore at all.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_uxo2_description: After <t %5>cluster munition</t> deployment, it is likely not all <t %5>submunitions</t> will have exploded. The target area may now contain hard-to-find <t %5>unexploded ordnance</t> (<t %5>UXO</t>). Like other <t %5>explosive remnants of war</t> (<t %5>ERW</t>), these explosives can cause harm to anyone in the area after deployment, including the original user and civilians.%1%1UXO can be carefully found and cleared by <t %5>specialists</t> using <t %5>Mine Detectors</t> and <t %5>Toolkits</t>.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_targetingcamera_t: Coupled with a laser designator, these cameras can be used to 'paint' targets for your weaponry or for other friendly units.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_targetingcamera_d: Some aircraft are equipped with high-magnification cameras with day, night and thermal modes.%1<t></t>1. Use %11 to switch to and from the targeting pod.%1<t></t>2. To stabilize the camera on an area press %12.%1<t></t>3. To re-center the camera to boresight or a marked target press %13.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_renegade_tip: Carefully identify your targets. Be aware of crossfire, projectile ricochets or penetrations, and indirect area of effect explosives!
str_a3_orange_cfghints_renegade_descript: Killing or destroying <t %5>unlawful targets</t> will have serious consequences. Repeatedly doing so will brand you an <t %5>enemy to everyone</t>. %11%1%1Unlawful targets include:%1%2 Civilians%1%2 Members of your faction%1%2 Members of allied factions
str_a3_orange_cfghints_renegade_arg11: Group leadership will be taken away from you, and even your own faction will use <t %5>lethal force</t> to stop you.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_premiumorange_des: %11%1%12%1%2"Remnants of War" - a singleplayer mini-campaign that explores the laws of armed conflict (LOAC)%1%2Showcases - a humanitarian NGO's open day, and VR LOAC instruction%1%2Time Trials - races against the clock using several types of vehicle%1%2International Development & Aid Project - the new civilian humanitarian Armaverse faction (IDAP)%1%2Van - a range of medium-sized wheeled transport vehicles, including ambulances%1%2Utility & Demining Drones - unmanned aerial vehicles for small payload delivery and remote minefield clearance%1%2APERS Mine Dispenser - an effective but controversial area denial weapon system%1%2Cluster Bombs & UXO - aircraft-delivered submunition containers that may leave behind unexploded ordnance after strikes%1%2Vests - safety, identification, multi-pocket and EOD vests%1%2Bags - messenger and leg strap bags%1%2Headgear - safari and hard hats, head bandages, basic and press helmets, ear protectors and a wireless earpiece%1%2Facewear - respirators and safety goggles%1%2Humanitarian Aid Objects - cardboard boxes, food sacks, water bottle packages, emergency blankets, and more%1%2Tent Objects - (medical) shelter tents, separate floor canvases, an air-conditioning unit, and plastic net fences%1%2Medical Objects - stretchers, IV bags, body bags, and more%1%2Furniture Objects - tables, a sofa, an armchair, a bed, and more%1%2Miscellaneous - a paramedic outfit, construction coveralls, and a training mine%1%2Official Soundtrack - newly composed music tracks%1%2Achievements - a set of extra Steam Achievements

str_a3_orange_cfghints_minesweep_descrip: Nearby mines can be detected by moving slowly and carefully looking around you. %14 Having a Mine Detector in your inventory will locate even well-hidden mines in your vicinity. Audio cues may alert you to such threats.%1%2Use %11 or %12 to bring up the Mines info panel to see approximate mine locations and identified mines.%1%2Carefully approach, look at, and identify unknown mines using %13.%1Depending on difficulty options, known mines are marked .
str_a3_orange_cfghints_minesweep_arg14: Mines may be harder to spot at night, from vehicles, or in bushes and grass. Some units have received training to be more adept at visual identification.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_minedispensers_ti: It is safe to disperse while standing nearby and behind the dispenser. The device can also be deactivated.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_minedispensers_de: The <t %5>APERS Mine Dispenser</t> differs from other placed weapon systems in that it is not itself an explosive device. It launches <t %5>14 APERS mines</t> into an <t %5>arc-shaped area</t>, extending approximately <t %5>20 meters</t> in the direction of placement. %11%1%2Place the device using the <t %5>Put</t> action.%1%2Add 40 s timer steps for delayed dispersal.%1%2Or disperse immediately / remotely using the <t %5>Touch off</t> action.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_minedispensers_ar: These dispensed mines become active on impact.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_leaflets_tip: Armed forces sometimes use leaflets to warn a local population of an impending military attack.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_leaflets_hintread: %12%1%1Leaflets found on the ground can be inspected by holding %11.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_leaflets_hintdrop: %12%1%1%2Specially equipped vehicles, such as Utility Drones, can release a stack of leaflets over an area.%1%2Fly to a reasonable altitude (around 30 meters), and release the leaflets by pressing %11.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_leaflets_descript: %13%1%1%2Specially equipped vehicles, such as Utility Drones, can release a stack of leaflets over an area.%1%2Fly to a reasonable altitude (around 30 meters), and release the leaflets by pressing %11.%1%1Leaflets found on the ground can be inspected by holding %12.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_leaflets_arg13: Simple paper leaflets can be distributed to <t %5>provide (mis)information</t> to anyone reading them.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_treatiesproto: IHL can also be referred to as jus in bello - the law which regulates the conduct of war. Serious violations are called war crimes. States must establish laws to try and punish those who commit grave breaches of IHL. Military commanders should instruct IHL and report violations. The rules seem straightforward, but the application of IHL to real-life situations of conflict often creates dilemmas.

The <t %5>legal framework</t> for IHL is defined in a set of <t %5>treaties</t> and <t %5>protocols</t>, more of which are being drafted to this day. While some have been ratified universally, others are still not observed by major nation states.%1%1Relevant examples include:%1%2<t %5>Geneva Conventions</t> - the best known and most widely adopted treaties, focuses on humanitarian treatment in war%1%2<t %5>Ottawa Treaty</t> - seeks to ban the use of all anti-personnel mines%1%2<t %5>Convention on Cluster Munitions</t> - prohibits the use of submunition-based weapons%1%2<t %5>Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons</t> - restricts the use of conventional weapons which are indiscriminate or cause excessive injuries
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_protectionpro: When civilians take a direct part in fighting, they lose their protection from attack (when in doubt, they should be considered civilian). When a civilian object is used in support of military action, it becomes a legitimate military target and loses its protection (when in doubt, it should be considered civilian). Protect the most vulnerable: civilians, wounded and sick, detainees, and health-care workers (such as IDAP)!

It is <t %5>forbidden</t> to:%1%2 attack civilians and civilian objects (houses, schools, places of worship, cultural or historic monuments, etc.)%1%2 commit murder or torture%1%2 commit acts of sexual violence%1%2 forcibly displace and starve civilians%1%2 attack hospitals, ambulances and health-care workers%1%2 use human shields%1%2 destroy stocks of food, farming areas, and the water supply%1%2 recruit or use children under the age of 15 in armed conflict%1%2 misuse the Red Crystal, Red Cross and Red Crescent%1%2 interfere with the delivery of humanitarian aid%1%2 damage the environment
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_protectionobl: <t %5>Captured civilians and enemy combatants</t>:%1%2must be given adequate food, water, clothing, shelter and medical care%1%2must be allowed to have contact with their families%1%1<t %5>Children and women</t> must be detained separately from men, to the extent feasible.%1%1<t %5>Enemy combatants</t> who are wounded, sick, shipwrecked, or surrendering:%1%2 must be searched for, collected and cared for%1%2 must not receive preferential treatment, except on medical grounds%1%1A <t %5>surrendering enemy</t> must not be wounded or killed.%1%1The specific protection, health and assistance needs of <t %5>women affected by armed conflict</t> must be respected.%1%1Everyone is entitled to a <t %5>fair trial</t>.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_proportionali: A target must still be military (legitimate)!

When collateral damage cannot be fully avoided, the expected number of deaths or injuries to civilians or damage to civilian objects must <t %5>not be excessive</t> compared to the anticipated military advantage. The advantage has to be <t %5>concrete</t> and cannot be "winning the war" for example.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_precaution_ti: Precaution applies not only during planning stages, but all the way up to the moment of an attack and even after it has commenced.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_precaution_de: All feasible measures should be taken to <t %5>avoid collateral damage</t>.%1%1This may include determining:%1%2 <t %5>When</t> to strike a target%1%2 <t %5>Where</t> to strike a target%1%2 <t %5>What</t> weapon systems to use against a target
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_overview_tip: IHL is often also referred to as rules of war, laws of war, or laws of armed conflict (LOAC).
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_overview_desc: %11%1%1IHL strikes a balance between the principle of <t %5>humanity</t> and <t %5>military necessity</t>.%1%1Key aspects include the <t %5>principles</t> of:%1%2 Humanity%1%2 Distinction%1%2 Precaution%1%2 Proportionality
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_overview_arg1: <t %5>International Humanitarian Law (IHL)</t> is a set of rules that aim to preserve <t %5>human dignity</t> in <t %5>armed conflict</t> by <t %5>protecting</t> the most vulnerable persons and by <t %5>limiting</t> the way in which war is conducted.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_moreinfo_tip: The in-game descriptions of IHL do not cover all details and complexities of the topic; they are merely an introduction. Please refer to other sources for a more comprehensive overview.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_moreinfo_desc: International Humanitarian Law is a complex topic that evolves alongside the nature of armed conflict. Please visit this web page for more information and links to relevant sources.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_limitsprohibi: It is <t %5>forbidden</t> to:%1%2 use weapons that cause unnecessary suffering (such as poison, blinding laser weapons or nuclear weapons)%1%2 use weapons that cannot distinguish between civilians and military targets (such as landmines)%1%2 take hostages%1%2 pretend to be a civilian while attempting to kill, injure or capture an adversary%1%2 order or threaten that there shall be no survivors
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_limitsobligat: Those who are fighting must <t %5>distinguish</t> themselves from those who are not.%1%1Attacks must be <t %5>limited to military objectives</t>.%1%1During an attack, every <t %5>precaution</t> must be taken to minimize potential harm to civilians and civilian objects.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_humanity_tip: A humanitarian act is an act carried out to protect someone whose life or human dignity is in danger, especially someone whom one would not ordinarily be inclined to help or protect. Such acts are likely to involve personal or material risk.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_humanity_desc: Civilians and wounded, sick, captured or surrendering combatants must be <t %5>treated humanely</t>.%1%1There are <t %5>limits on the means and methods of war</t> to avoid unnecessary suffering.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_distinction_t: Huge quantities of explosive remnants of war, such as mines and cluster bomblets, are still scattered across historical conflict zones to this day.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_distinction_d: Military operations should only be carried out against <t %5>combatants</t> and <t %5>military targets</t>.%1%1Those who are fighting must <t %5>distinguish</t> themselves from those who are not.%1%1Weapons that cannot distinguish between civilians and military targets are forbidden.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_definitions_t: When civilians take a direct part in fighting, they lose their protection from attack (when in doubt, they should be considered civilian). When a civilian object is used in support of military action, it becomes a legitimate military target and loses its protection (when in doubt, it should be considered civilian).
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ihl_definitions_d: %2 <t %5>Combatant</t>: members of armed forces, members of any armed group under the orders of a party to a conflict%1%2 <t %5>Hors de combat</t>: "out of fight" - combatants who have been captured or wounded or who are sick or shipwrecked and thus no longer in a position to fight%1%2 <t %5>Civilian</t>: any person who is not a combatant%1%2 <t %5>Armed conflict</t>: fighting between countries (international) or between a country's armed forces and armed groups (non-international) or between such groups%1%2 <t %5>Military objective</t>: an object that by its nature, location, purpose or use makes an effective contribution to military action and whose destruction offers a definite military advantage%1%2 <t %5>Non-reciprocity</t>: breaches of IHL by one party to a conflict do not justify breaches by other parties%1%2 <t %5>Equality</t>: IHL applies to all parties of an armed conflict equally
str_a3_orange_cfghints_dlcstrategy_tip: You can try premium assets in the Virtual Arsenal mode without restriction!
str_a3_orange_cfghints_dlcstrategy_descr: Arma 3's DLC strategy﻿ is based on 3 main pillars:%1%2 Providing free platform updates%1%2 Offering new premium content%1%2 Preventing multiplayer fragmentation%1%1With this approach, every Arma 3 player gets all the DLC data and is able to see everything in-game. Generally speaking, features continue expanding the platform and are free for all to enjoy, while the premium content may be limited for non-owners. By purchasing DLC you are contributing to further development of a consistent Arma 3 platform for everyone and the Arma series in general. Thank you!
str_a3_orange_cfghints_combatmodes_tip: Controlling RoE will let you set ambushes and avoid undesired escalations.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_combatmodes_descr: %12%1%2%13%1%2%14%1%2%15%1%1The available combat modes are:%1%2Open fire - units will fire at any suitable target in range%1%2Hold fire - units will not fire at will, unless explicitly ordered to do so%1%2Fire - units will eliminate only assigned targets
str_a3_orange_cfghints_combatmodes_arg15: Select the desired mode from the list.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_combatmodes_arg14: Press %3[3]%4 to bring up the list of modes.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_combatmodes_arg12: As commander you have control over the <t %5>combat mode</t> (<t %5>Rules of Engagement</t>) of your subordinate units:
str_a3_orange_cfghints_clustermunitions_: Depending on the munition, dispersal altitude and other factors, many submunitions do not initially explode. They stay behind on the battlefield and cause harm for long periods of time.

Cluster munitions are <t %5>containers</t> which are launched over a target area, and then opened to disperse a large number of smaller <t %5>bomblets</t> (<t %5>submunitions</t>). Methods of container delivery include dropping as <t %5>aircraft cluster bomb</t> or firing as <t %5>artillery shell</t>. These munitions have a large area of effect and cause <t %5>indiscriminate destruction</t>.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ccoc_protectivesy: <t %5>Symbols</t> such as the Red Crystal, Red Cross and Red Crescent should be <t %5>respected</t>.%1%11%1%1They protect:%1%2 Medical staff%1%2 Ambulances and relief transports%1%2 Hospitals and first-aid posts
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ccoc_prisonersofw: Captured and surrendered enemy combatants should be <t %5>treated humanely</t>.%1%1%2 Spare them.%1%2 Disarm them.%1%2 Hand them over to a superior.%1%2 Treat them humanely.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ccoc_horsdecombat: Don't target those who are hors de combat!

When combatants are <t %5>hors de combat</t> ("out of fight": e.g. wounded, captured, sick or shipwrecked), they should <t %5>not be targeted</t>.%1%1%2 Collect them.%1%2 Care for them.%1%2 Hand them over to a superior or nearest medical personnel.%1%2 Respect medical personnel, facilities and any civilians helping.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ccoc_combatrules_: Always keep these basic rules in mind:%1%2 Fight only <t %5>combatants</t>.%1%2 Attack only <t %5>military targets</t>.%1%2 <t %5>Spare civilian</t> persons and objects.%1%2 <t %5>Limit destruction</t> to what your mission requires.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ccoc_civilians_ti: Protect civilians and treat them with respect!
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ccoc_civilians_de: Non-combatants such as civilians should <t %5>never</t> be <t %5>targeted</t>.%1%1%2 Respect them.%1%2 Treat them humanely.%1%2 Protect them.%1%2 Respect their property.
str_a3_orange_cfghints_ammotype_descript: Artillery operates with several different ammo types:%1%2HE shells - simple explosive ammo%1%2Flares - used for signaling%1%2Smoke shells - for signaling or screening%1%2Guided - heat seeking shells%1%2Laser Guided - precise, guided by laser designation%1%2Mines - clusters of AP or AT mines%1%2Cluster shells - exploding submunition containers
str_a3_orange_cfghints_disarm: To deactivate an explosive, you have to be a specialist, such as an %3Explosive / EOD Specialist%4 or an %3Engineer%4, and have a %3Toolkit%4.%1%2You may have to manually reveal %12 the explosive first.%1%2Crawl %11 to the explosive.%1%2Select %3Deactivate%4 from the action menu.%1WARNING: if you don't approach the explosive carefully in a prone position, it may detonate.

str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_orange_pare_foo: We hope you'll enjoy this special release as much as we've enjoyed creating it!
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_orange_pare: Arma 3 Laws of War is composed of the following premium content and free platform additions:
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_orange_pard_lis: we've added Field Manual records covering the Laws of Armed Conflict, and made small sandbox tweaks to improve our representation of LOAC.
drop informational pamphlets from the sky and apply your own designs for your scenarios.
detection of mines and other explosives is a little more involved now, by using a new info panel and manual identification.
submunition technology now has additional randomization options, aircraft bombs and mines are supported, and unexploded ordnance may be left behind after deployment.
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_orange_pard: Above all, this DLC set out to add assets and content, but we have also done some modest <t color='%1'>feature extensions</t> and improvements during its development, free for everyone, of course:
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_orange_parc_foo: More about Arma 3 Laws of War
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_orange_parc: Continuing our established DLC strategy, we are bringing DLC owners a varied collection of premium content. While portions of the new civilian International Development & Aid Project (IDAP) faction are free for the platform, we've selected several new assets to make them a special and worthwhile addition. IDAP's primary ground vehicle is a large Van, available for passenger transport, cargo hauling and medical evacuations. In order to safely carry out their activities in high-risk areas, IDAP also uses several drones. The Utility Drone is its latest acquisition and they have even modified it for remote mine clearance. A wide range of IDAP and other character gear is further available for anyone wishing to wear it. Much to IDAP's frustration, military factions have started to use a particularly nasty weapon: the APERS Mine Dispenser. These and all the extra platform additions are showcased in the singleplayer "Remnants of War" mini-campaign, and as always: get a hands-on preview without restriction in the Virtual Arsenal mode.
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_orange_parb2: We've always admired this pragmatic approach to a complex topic. Rather than frustrate players with punishments and mandatory lessons, our mutual goal has been to find ways of raising awareness of IHL, while creating an even deeper and more authentic Arma experience. To that end we decided to build a DLC around IHL, which primarily delivers an Armaverse humanitarian NGO faction and gameplay to showcase them. We will also be donating a portion of the 2017 DLC proceeds to the ICRC so that they may continue their good real-world work. Thank you for your support!
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_orange_parb: For some time now we've had an inspirational working relationship with the <t color='%1'>International Committee of the Red Cross</t> (ICRC). Especially in recent years, they have identified games as a valid vehicle to spread awareness of a topic that both makes sense to everyone, yet can be very complicated to explain, implement and safeguard. We're talking about <t color='%1'>International Humanitarian Law</t> (IHL), also known as the laws of armed conflict, the rules of war, or the laws of war. Its most widely known component is perhaps the Geneva Conventions. The ICRC has helped our developers to be educated on this important aspect of warfare, and they have pointed out how we might improve our games to include IHL elements, without taking fun away from players.
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_orange_para: It is with some pride that we welcome you to the release of the Arma 3 Laws of War DLC. Known for some time under code name "Orange" on our 2017 roadmap, we have recently revealed the unique theme of this asset and content pack to you all. We feel there is something for everyone to be found in this DLC and the accompanying platform update. So we invite you to keep reading for more information, or to dive straight into the game and explore the additions for yourself. This is war!

str_a3_tanks_m02_mission:
Although NATO have taken ground, they have not yet readied their defenses. If we act quickly, we may be able push them back and delay their attack on %2Pyrgos%1.

The town of %3Dorida%1 is our primary objective.

If we secure it and break through their lines, we can disrupt logistics and devastate their beachhead. However, watch out for civilians. There are hundreds of refugees fleeing south; so be sure you identify your targets.

str_a3_tanks_m02_diary:
Last night I dreamt of fire.

On the digital displays, my father's olive grove was burning. No sound, no screams, no chatter on the radio. Just the gentle hum of our engine. And across from me, my crew, calm, indifferent. Fanning cards and nodding, absentmindedly.

I awoke on our back deck.

Everything seemed normal. There was the familiar smell of damp webbing and diesel on the breeze. But I knew from the silence something wasn't right. Our driver, Leventis, was already on his feet, washing from an empty ammo box. He stood staring into the distance, watching plumes of smoke rise lazily to greet the morning sun. The scene, deceptively peaceful.

Sometime before dawn, the Americans captured Dorida. Today we'll take it back.

K.

str_a3_tanks_m02_debriefing02: A resounding victory, to be sure - but your methods? They're questionable. I can only hope reports, citing civilian deaths, are no more than baseless lies, propagated by the enemy.
str_a3_tanks_m02_debriefing01: A resounding victory, excellent job! It'll take time before NATO can regain momentum. But make no mistake: we'll need more than superior battle tanks if we're to win this war.

str_a3_tanks_m02_intro_05_01: Needless to say, the conflict that followed? It didn't go well.
str_a3_tanks_m02_intro_01_02: And our government became subservient to the will of foreign powers.
str_a3_tanks_m02_intro_04: NATO were helping the guerrillas: when they attacked, we hit back - and they responded with a whole invasion force.
str_a3_tanks_m02_intro_02_01: Distrusting the Americans, we aligned ourselves with the Canton Strategic Alliance Treaty.
str_a3_tanks_m02_intro_03_02: I mean, we didn't know it then, but, we were caught in a whirlwind; a series of events we could scarcely comprehend.
str_a3_tanks_m02_intro_02_02: They gave us technology, weapons. Economic and political support - and in return, we allowed them to use our island.

str_a3_tanks_m03_situation:
The end has come.

Colonel Akhanteros is about to announce our surrender.

But first we must oversee a successful rearguard action. CSAT are evacuating scientists and sensitive material via the %2airfield near Selakano%1. It's our job to ensure they leave our island safely. Exactly what it's all about, I cannot say. But the orders are clear and come from the very top. This mission is important.

str_a3_tanks_m03_overviewtext: Hours before an expected ceasefire, the AAF make a stand against overwhelming odds.
str_a3_tanks_m03_mission:
Move up from %2Point Delta%1 and wait for the Americans; we must delay them for as long as possible - use whatever strategy you like, Captain, just don't let them get by you.

As your CO was injured earlier today, you will take charge of his Angara. It is a 'command' variant and boasts an extra turret-mounted, 30mm autocannon. But remember, like the standard model, its armor plating's top secret. CSAT made it very clear. If one of their tanks is knocked out or immobilized, we must scuttle it before our enemies can investigate. After completing your mission, you will need to use the explosives, located in your storage bins, to destroy your own.

Good luck.
str_a3_tanks_m03_execution:
1. Get in your %2T-140K Angara%1.
2. Move to a strategic position.
3. Drive back all attacking forces.
str_a3_tanks_m03_diary:
I'm still alive.

Tomorrow's close.

CSAT need us to buy them time. And as we are an army of none, a marionette and not a nation, we must dance to their tune. If our strings are cut, we collapse.

Every minute's a victory. Every second, a moment won. Hour hands are a stay of execution; a reprieve. I don't know which - and that's a thing of fear. Now we fight, not for the Republic but for the terms of our surrender.

Fate smiles, but I can make no sense of her.

I'm told our chances are one in three. Either I will make it home or, these words will find you. Just know: nothing's been left unsaid.

K.
str_a3_tanks_m03_debriefing03: A noble effort. However, we were quickly overcome and the enemy hindered CSAT's evacuation efforts. Hopefully they will overlook this failure and will continue to support us in the difficult days ahead.
str_a3_tanks_m03_debriefing02: Thanks to your heroism and decisive action, our forces held the line. Unfortunately, we believe NATO are in possession of an Angara battle tank. If CSAT learn of this, it could cause problems in the difficult days ahead.
str_a3_tanks_m03_debriefing01: Thanks to your heroism and decisive action, our forces held the line. Honestly, you couldn't have done more. The secret components of CSAT's tanks are safe and their evacuation was a complete success. You have singlehandedly turned a catastrophe into a valiant defeat.
str_a3_tanks_m03_intro_04: Few imagined it would end this way - fewer still, imagined we'd make a difference.
str_a3_tanks_m03_intro_01_01: The fighting that ensued was brutal.
str_a3_tanks_m03_intro_03_02: So, we retreated south and organized our lines of defense.
str_a3_tanks_m03_intro_01_02: Our forces, they held out for several days, even though we had no hope of victory.
str_a3_tanks_m03_intro_03_01: They needed more time, and we promised to give it to 'em.
str_a3_tanks_m03_intro_02_01: The only chance we had was CSAT.
str_a3_tanks_m03_intro_02_02: Their tanks were precious but their influence at a future negotiating table was vital.
str_a3_tanks_m03_outro_06b_02: Summoning all my courage before the rattle of keys, the blindfold, a last command.
str_a3_tanks_m03_outro_01: Somehow, I survived that final battle...
str_a3_tanks_m03_outro_06b_01: Now - as a prisoner - I await my fate.
str_a3_tanks_m03_outro_01a: Against the odds, we stood our ground. Facing death, moments before a ceasefire.
str_a3_tanks_m03_outro_06a_02: I quit the army and came home, leaving all I could of the war behind me.
str_a3_tanks_m03_outro_01b: The odds had been against us; we did everything we could.
str_a3_tanks_m03_outro_06a_01: After two months, we were released.
str_a3_tanks_m03_outro_05b: They singled me out, claiming I had murdered civilians...
str_a3_tanks_m03_outro_02_02: But we came off the worst. Over a third of our forces were either dead or wounded.
str_a3_tanks_m03_outro_05a: They had no interest in me, a simple tank commander.
str_a3_tanks_m03_outro_03a: And as for those Angara tanks? We destroyed 'em, not a single one was captured.
str_a3_tanks_m03_outro_05: There, the guerrillas worked with NATO, identifying war criminals among our ranks.
str_a3_tanks_m03_outro_03b: And as for those Angara tanks? Well, at least one was captured by the Americans.
str_a3_tanks_m03_outro_04: Some time later, we were rounded up and taken to an internment camp.

str_a3_tanks_m01_situation:
Since the destruction of Oreokastro and the limitations to NATO's mandate, the Freedom and Independence Army have grown in strength. Our morale is weak. Our own people are against us. Reports of desertion and sabotage are rife.

If we are to defeat this insurgency, we cannot waste our time, severing heads from the hydra. Instead, we must cauterize its wounds - drain the swamp - isolate the enemy and tighten our grip on those areas where they are strongest.

%2Checkpoint Sigma%1 just checked in.

Apparently, they have some intel on guerrilla activity. My guess, it's another bootless errand, but, you never know.

And seeing as you're heading out that way, %3Observation Post Omega%1 require a carburetor for their generator. The damn thing's broken down again.

str_a3_tanks_m01_diary:
That pebble you gave me, on the beach near Edessa.

You swore it could teach me everything worth learning in life. You said it was a perfect creature. Equal to itself, mindful of its limits.

I remember you shrugging your shoulders, walking on, as I made a move to throw it back into the sea. Now I think I understand. Or at least, in part.

The world will not change me.

And things here? They demand a cold, resilient eye. Someone must bear witness. The violence, it's born of frustration. Our forces scour the forests and mountains, finding nothing. We are like an army, marching out against the wind - a great colossus, punching air.

I don't see a war, not really. I see acts of madness. Meaningless dead, young martyrs; black with blood and white with lime, rolled on boot heels into early graves. Our enemy have a cause, while we have only orders. It seems in a clenched fist, your pebble's warmth is false. And I am glad.

K.

str_a3_tanks_m01_intro_01: My name is Kyros Kalogeros. I was born in Kavala, at the turn of the millennium.

str_a3_tanks_m01_intro_05_02: Repression stoked the flames of resistance and, six months later, the situation exploded.
str_a3_tanks_m01_intro_03_02: Looking back now, during the peace, I never believed my skills would be needed.

Having secured a foothold earlier today on the %2Eastern Penninsula%1, we are now poised to push farther south, towards the city of %3Paros%1.
%17%17The enemy's %4defensive line%1, east of the %5main airport%1, is still our main objective. If we can exploit their positions %6here%1, they'll be forced to respond, splitting their forces to fight on two fronts.
%17%17Our close air support has already wreaked some havoc. The %7radar station%1 and %8military base%1 in the area have both been destroyed - but armored threats remain, particularly in places with a high risk of civilian casualties.
%17%17MBTs from %9Zulu%1 then, will advance south, parallel to the %10main highway%1, while callsigns %11Charlie%1 and %12Yankee%1, with a supporting tank destroyer from %13Victor%1, will move in tandem along our western flank, down through the forest valley, towards %15Point Yukon%1, avoiding the hybrid minefield, %18located here%1.
%17%17Once we've broken through, all elements will continue to %16Point Brazos%1, where we will begin the second phase of the operation.

str_a3_vanguard_tips_secure_time: *  Points are also allocated for killing enemies.
str_a3_vanguard_tips_secure:
Secure Device
* It is possible to win the mission and secure the device by eliminating opposing players. Consider your strength and adjust your plans accordingly.
str_a3_vanguard_tips_locate_time: * Be pro-active and stay on the move. Time is of the essence. A significant number of points are awarded to the team that first loads the device onto a truck.
str_a3_vanguard_tips_locate:
Locate Device
* Be sure to check your map for regular updates on the device's position.
* Move with caution inside the expected landing zone, there is a strong possibility enemies will be active there.
* Consider the risk of dividing your forces. On the one hand, you can cover more ground and increase the chances of retrieving the device quickly. On the other, players are more vulnerable in smaller numbers.
* Ensure a truck is ready to transport the device to safety; remember though, that such vehicles are priority targets for opposing teams.
str_a3_vanguard_tips_brif_phase:
Briefing Phase
* Communication is key. Once a team leader has been assigned, listen carefully to their instructions and work together to accomplish objectives.
* Draw lines on the map to communicate strategies and plans to other players on your team. Hold down the Left Ctrl button while viewing the map and draw a line by using the Left Mouse Button with cursor motion. To remove a line or marker you have placed, move the cursor to it and press Delete.
* Only select weapons and equipment appropriate for the mission or your role within it.
str_a3_vanguard_task1description: Your map will update every %1 minutes, as the area of the expected dropzone diminishes.
str_a3_vanguard_rules_wincondition_time: * As a team, hold the highest collective score before the mission time expires.
str_a3_vanguard_rules_scoring:
Scoring
Points are awarded per side as follows:
+ %1 for the first side who successfully loads the device onto a truck.
+ %2 for every opponent killed.
+ %3 for every %4 seconds the device is loaded in a truck with at least one friendly unit inside.
str_a3_vanguard_rules_no_ai: Disabled. If you would like to play with AI, you must enable them in the mission parameters
str_a3_vanguard_rules_leaders:
Team Leaders
Each side may have one player in command. Their role is to supervise the mission, allocating tasks and waypoints.
* Individual players may request or relinquish the command role by pressing and holding %1
* If two or more players wish to be team leaders, the player with the highest rank will be selected.
* If there are a number of players with the same rank who want the role, priority will be given to the player who requested the position first.
* If the mission begins without a commander, the first player to volunteer will automatically be chosen, regardless of their rank.
* Should a team leader be killed in action, the role will be given to a player who has logged their interest. Precedence will be given according to rank. If no other players are waiting, the position will be open.
* To create tasks as a team leader, press %2 to view the map and select friendly units by either clicking the left-mouse button on them or clicking it and dragging your cursor across them. You will see these units have been highlighted. Next, click the left-mouse button once more to place a task for the units selected. By default, tasks are labelled MOVE, but more appropriate task titles can be found by right clicking on the created task.
str_a3_vanguard_rules_basic: The device is in the air and will arrive by parachute. The dropzone, represented by the circle on your map, will decrease by increments as the mission progresses. All sides receive updates, revealing the location or expected location of the objective. Cooperate with team members and use the vehicles available to complete the mission.
str_a3_vanguard_rules_ai_description:
Individual players are allocated a finite number of AI team mates.
If you are killed in action, you may assume control of one of your subordinates. These supporting units are divided evenly between players. However, if this is not possible, they will be allocated according to rank. Higher-ranking players will then benefit from any surplus figure.
