str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_tank_pard: Arma 3 Tanks is composed of the following premium content and free platform additions:
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_tank_parc_list6: a selection of missiles now features direct or top-down attack flight modes, plus support for terrain-following munitions has been added. A few weapons now also have the ability to lock-on after launch.
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_tank_parc_list5: armored vehicles can be customized in the Virtual Garage with additional armor protection and camouflage nets for better concealment in different terrains.
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_tank_parc_list4: the audio experience of armored vehicles is made more lifelike via the addition of more stereo sound samples, positional sounds, and more distinct audio cues for gearbox and RPM changes.
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_tank_parc_list3: armor now reacts more realistically to incoming rounds. For example, cage armor (also known as slat armor) is not just a visual object, but really does offer protection against RPGs.
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_tank_parc_list2: armored vehicles now feel more natural to drive thanks to improvements to the wheel collision simulation, the way different ground surfaces affect handling, and other changes.
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_tank_parc_list1: every armored vehicle in Arma 3 now features a fully 3D-modeled interior with Multi-Functional Displays and camera feeds for crew members.
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_tank_parc: We're excited to once again bring a significant range of <t color='%1'>free new features</t> to every Arma 3 player. Befitting the DLC theme, we've focused on an <t color='%1'>enhanced armored vehicle experience</t> for all relevant vehicles in the game (existing and new). These sandbox improvements have been on many wishlists for a long time and now they are finally here!
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_tank_parb: Just like every DLC before it, Arma 3 Tanks follows our well-established DLC strategy. Part of this approach is a collection of premium content for owners. They will find unrestricted access to 3 brand-new armored vehicles: the T-140 Angara Main Battle Tank, the Nyx Armored Weapons Carrier, and the Rhino MGS Tank Destroyer (all with multiple variants). They were designed to complement the existing factions, where each plays a specific role in the intricate armored warfare spectrum. Get to know these very different vehicles and their unique capabilities while playing the "Altis Requiem" mini-campaign and Showcase Tank Destroyers. Not an owner yet, but curious to try the premium vehicles? Boot up Virtual Garage mode to go hands-on without restriction.
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_tank_para: Roll in heavy firepower and take control of the battlefield with three brand new armored vehicles in the <t color='%1'>Arma 3 Tanks</t> DLC. Read on for a peak under the hood of these metal beasts now available to the DLC owners, and to check what impressive additions and tweaks have been included within the associated platform update for each and every player. When you're done here, head on over to the in-game motor pool and start revving some engines!
str_a3_warheadtypes3: Composite armor is significantly more effective against HEAT munitions than kinetic energy penetrators.
str_a3_warheadtypes2: Modern military forces use different munition types against different targets. For example:%1%2%3AP, APDS, APFSDS%4 - various types of armor piercing munitions that rely upon simple kinetic energy to penetrate armor%1%2%3HE%4 - high-explosive fragmentation rounds, used against infantry and unarmored targets%1%2%3HEAT%4 - High-Explosive Anti-Tank rounds use chemical energy to penetrate armor%1%2%3Tandem HEAT%4 - a HEAT round with a small precursor warhead to defeat the reactive armor of the target
str_a3_vorona_library1: 9M135 Vorona (NATO's reporting name: AT-19 Sweeper) is one of the newest ATGMs developed for CSAT's infantry and motorized units. The maximum range of this subsonic manual-guided missile is 2000 m, regardless of the time of day or weather conditions. This is because the command launch unit features powerful optics with day and infra-red vision modes and a laser rangefinder. The launcher can even be used without a tripod, and can be mounted on vehicles like the Qilin light strike vehicle. Two 130mm missiles are currently available; anti-tank with a powerful tandem HEAT warhead, and anti-personnel with a HE-FRAG warhead.
str_a3_slatarmor3: Slat armor adds significant weight to the vehicle. In addition, it increases a vehicle's size, meaning they may be too bulky for transportation in other vehicles. Driving can also become more challenging.
str_a3_slatarmor2: Slat (or cage) armor helps to defeat incoming HEAT rounds by detonating them before reaching the vehicle armor itself.%1However, it has zero effect against armor-piercing shells and can be damaged easily, leaving the underlaying part vulnerable to repeated attacks.
str_a3_rhino_library1: The Rhino MGS is the latest wheeled tank destroyer in NATO armored forces, designed for easy transportation to crisis regions. Its lightweight 120mm main cannon can use all conventional rounds including MARUK ATGMs, which increase its effective range to 8 km. The vehicle's secondary weapon is the .338 magnum SPMG coaxial machinegun. The price paid for the Rhino's great mobility and firepower is its light armor and low supplies of ammo and fuel. The 'UP' version is equipped with a remotely operated 12.7mm HMG and improved protection, provided by a cage and reactive armor. However, with this setup, it's too bulky to fit into many transport vehicles, including the Blackfish VTOL.
str_a3_reactivearmor3: The ERA layer adds significant weight to the vehicle, affecting its maneuverability.
str_a3_reactivearmor2: Explosive reactive armor affords extra protection against HEAT warheads. However, it's a one-time solution. When hit, the respective part of the vehicle will be left unprotected.%1To defeat ERA, tandem HEAT warheads were developed - a smaller warhead detonates the ERA while the main charge detonates on the vehicle itself.
str_a3_nyx_library1: The AWC 300 Nyx family consists of a number of light, fast and agile combat vehicles used by the AAF. While small and lightly armored, the Nyx can surprise enemies by striking from unexpected positions with its decent and accurate firepower. The anti-tank and air-defense variants are equipped with IR guided missiles and a 12.7mm HMG. The strike variant uses a 20mm autocannon and a 7.62mm coaxial machinegun. The recon variant is unarmed, but uses its radar and sensors to detect nearby threats and pass target data to friendly units via data link. It can also paint targets with its laser designator, which is located on a telescopic mount.
str_a3_missileflightmodes3: Top-down and overfly modes need a certain distance from the target if they are to be used. If the target is too close, direct mode is used.
str_a3_missileflightmodes2: Modern guided missiles can operate in different flight modes, allowing their user to increase their effectiveness against the selected target.%1%2%3Direct%4 - missile flies directly towards the target %1%2%3Top-down%4 - missile gains altitude after launch and descends from above %1%2%3Overfly top-attack%4 - missile flies and detonates directly above the target %1%2%3Terrain copy%4 - missile copies the terrain until reaching the target area
str_a3_maaws_library1: The MAAWS Mk4 (Multi-role Anti-armor Anti-tank Weapon System) is the latest member of the originally Swedish-made recoilless rifle family. The Mk4 is lighter, accurate, and more durable than its predecessors. It can fire multiple types of 84mm rounds, with a maximum effective range of 700 meters against static targets. The Mod 0 uses a simple daytime optical sight, while the Mod 1 has a laser rangefinder and integrated night-vision to accurately engage enemy targets at various ranges, at any hour of the day.
str_a3_loal3: Explosive munitions can have unintended consequences. Always make sure there are no friendly units in the target area before firing.
str_a3_loal2: Some guided missiles are able to lock-on after launch (LOAL) and can be used against targets beyond immediate line of sight.%1%2Press %11 to pick a desired target. This gives the missile an initial position to fly to.%1%2Select appropriate fire mode %12 to clear terrain between you and the target, if needed (top or terrain-following if available).%1%2Fire the missile in the target's direction.%1%1The missile will now fly towards the marked position. If no target was marked, then the position under the crosshair or a preset distance is used. Once there, the missile will try to lock on the nearest available target within the seeker's field of regard.
str_a3_compositearmor2: Modern armored fighting vehicles usually use composite armor, which is more effective in defeating HEAT munitions compared to simple steel armor.%1Composite armor, however, needs to be thick enough to achieve its purpose, meaning it's usually used on the front and sides of main battle tanks, leaving other parts more vulnerable to RPGs and ATGMs.
str_a3_cfghints_premiumcontent_premiumta: %11%1%12%1%2T-140 Angara – CSAT’s most formidable battle tank, unrivaled in firepower and armor. Features a Commander variant and multiple liveries.%1%2AWC Nyx – small in size, this flexible tankette punches well above its weight; with four variants, it’s suited to multiple forms of warfare, including recon, anti-tank, and even anti-air roles!%1%2Rhino MGS – a steel beast designed for one purpose – to destroy other tanks! Armed with a mighty 120mm cannon, it can dispense many types of rounds, including the new MARUK anti-tank guided missile. Also comes with a UP variant.%1%2"Altis Requiem" – play as an AAF tank commander and take control of an AWC Nyx, and later, the T-140 Angara, in this explosive, three-mission mini-campaign.%1%2Showcase Tank Destroyers – climb in NATO’s primary tank destroyer and utilize its speed and agility to outmaneuver the deadliest of armored adversaries.%1%2"Vanguard" – a team-vs-team multiplayer mode that focuses on tactics, group cohesion, and Arma 3’s combined arms gameplay.%1%2Time Trials – put the new Angara, Nyx, and Rhino to the test in three speedy time trial races across Altis and Malden.%1%2"9M135" Vorona – a manually guided missile launcher, replete with powerful optics, thermal imaging, and a laser rangefinder.%1%2MAAWS Mk4 – an unguided recoilless rifle, available in the older Mod 0 version used by AAF and FIA, and the newer Mod 1 version, employed by NATO.%1%2Anti-Tank Vehicle Variants – enjoy variants of the existing Offroad, Prowler, and Qilin LSVs that come equipped with mounted launchers.%1%2Tank Crew Clothing – unique CSAT tank crew helmet and AAF tank crew overalls.%1%2Decorative Objects – new decorative objects for Arma 3 content creators, such as tank defenses, spare parts, tools, and a fully functional repair depot.%1%2Official Soundtrack – listen to newly composed music tracks.%1%2Achievements – a set of extra Steam Achievements.
str_a3_angara_library1: A licensed variant of the original Russian design operated by the elite of CSAT armored forces. The tank is equipped with a high velocity, high-accuracy 125mm cannon, a 7.62mm coaxial machinegun, and a 12.7mm HMG in a remote turret. The crew is located in an armored capsule in the hull, improving survivability and eliminating one of the weaknesses of older tank designs. The disadvantage is its technical complexity and cost, resulting in low production numbers. Two main variants are currently in use - the standard T-140 and the T-140K, a 'commander' variant which exchanges the HMG for a 30mm autocannon. In addition, it also provides additional radios and sensors for platoon and company leaders.

STR_A3_VR_objWHA1_1_desc: Eliminate all virtual enemies. Note that hits do different damage based on where they hit the body. Use of body armor and helmets will reduce damage.
STR_A3_VR_objWHA2_1_desc: Neutralize the virtual enemy. As the target is close to you and moving at a slower rate, you don't have to lead too much in order to score a hit.
STR_A3_VR_objWHA2_2_desc: Neutralize the virtual enemy. As the distance to the target is considerably longer, hitting it will require more precise leading and timing of your shots.
STR_A3_VR_objWHA2_3_desc: Eliminate both virtual enemies circling around you in the quad bikes.
STR_A3_VR_objWHA2_4_desc: Shoot down both miniature UAVs. They present a small, fast moving target, which is difficult to hit. Weapons with a high rate of fire, such as machineguns, may make it considerably easier to hit such a target.
STR_A3_VR_objWHA3_1_desc:
Take the vest - it will come with some additional magazines.
The more protection the vests offer, the heavier they are and will significantly contribute to wearer's fatigue.
STR_A3_VR_objWHA3_2_desc: Take the backpack - it will come with 2 Medikits.
STR_A3_VR_objWHA3_3_desc: Move to the indicated position. Try to manage your fatigue and to arrive in a ready-to-fire condition.
STR_A3_VR_objWHA3_4_desc: Catch your breath and decrease your fatigue level. Lowering your weapon and going crouch/prone will decrease your fatigue faster.
STR_A3_VR_objWHA3_5_desc: Hit the indicated part of the target while keeping your fatigue low.
STR_A3_VR_objWHA3_6_desc: Hit the indicated part of the target while maintaining a medium fatigue level. Aiming will be more difficult, but you can hold your breath for temporary stabilization.
STR_A3_VR_objWHA3_7_desc: Hit the indicated part of the target while maintaining the maximum fatigue level. Aiming will be very difficult and you will only be able to hold your breath for a very short time period.
STR_A3_VR_objWHB1_1_desc: Enter the shooting range and prepare for a live fire exercise.
STR_A3_VR_objWHB1_2_desc: Move through the shooting range and eliminate all enemies. At the end, you'll see your average time needed to eliminate a target with your current weapon.
STR_A3_VR_objWHB1_3_desc: Move through the shooting range again with a more cumbersome weapon.
STR_A3_VR_objWHB2_1_desc: Adjust your stance so that you can see, and eliminate, the gunner on the other side of the wall.
STR_A3_VR_objWHB2_2_desc: Adjust your stance and eliminate both of the hidden enemies behind the low wall.
STR_A3_VR_objWHB3_1_desc: Move closer to the virtual blocks in front of you and deploy your machinegun.
STR_A3_VR_objWHB3_2_desc: Eliminate all enemy crewmen before they reach the tanks.
STR_A3_VR_objWHB3_3_desc: Aim your weapon over the virtual blocks to achieve a stable firing position.
STR_A3_VR_objWHB3_4_desc: Hit all targets from a stabilized position.

STR_A3_VR_objWHC1_2_desc: Switch to optics, zoom in and eliminate all targets along the northern tower.

STR_A3_VR_objWHC2_2_desc: Enter the shooting range and prepare for a live fore exercise.

str_a3_cfghints_premiumcontent_premiumma: Hone your shooting skills and engage in ranged combat with the seven new weapons in the Arma 3 Marksmen DLC.%1%1%2<\t>Weapon: Cyrus 9.3 mm%1%2<\t>Weapon: Mk14 7.62 mm%1%2<\t>Weapon: ASP-1 Kir 12.7 mm%1%2<\t>Weapon: SPMG .338%1%2<\t>Weapon: Navid 9.3 mm%1%2<\t>Weapon: MAR-10 .338%1%2<\t>Weapon: Mk-I EMR 7.62 mm%1%2<\t>Character: Sniper - with a new full ghillie suit%1%2<\t>Character: Grenadier - with a new heavy vest%1%2<\t>3 Singleplayer Firing Drills%1%2<\t>End Game - a team based multiplayer mode%1%2<\t>Showcase Firing From Vehicles%1%2<\t>Showcase Marksmen%1%2<\t>VR Training courses%1%2<\t>Remote Designators%1%2<\t>Laser Designators%1%2<\t>Facepaints - 9 faces with camouflage%1%2<\t>Kahlia Scope%1%2<\t>AMS Scope%1%2<\t>Weapon Accessories%1%2<\t>Firing Drills Decorative Objects%1%2<\t>Set of extra Steam Achievements%1<\t>
STR_A3_TargetLeading2: To hit a moving target, you have to lead it correctly. The main factors influencing your success are:%1%2Distance to the target%1%2The target's velocity%1%2Your weapon's muzzle velocity%1%2The ballistic trajectory of the round
STR_A3_TargetLeading3: Practice makes master, especially in this case.
STR_A3_AVCamera2: When you are connected to a UAV or remote designator, you can activate a live feed.%1%2Use %11 to toggle the live camera feed on and off.
STR_A3_WeaponInertia2: Weapon inertia simulates the lateral movement incurred while turning around with your weapon. The heavier the weapon, the more time it takes for the shooter to properly re-align their sights.%1%1This means that lighter weapons, like pistols or SMGs, have advantages over rifles, in CQB, or machineguns, in faster target acquisition.
STR_A3_WeaponInertia3: Weapon attachments effect inertia as well. While heavier optics or suppressors will increase inertia, some grips or handles will actually decrease it.
STR_A3_Ballistics2: Bullets have accurately simulated ballistic trajectories. The more powerful round, and the longer the weapon's barrel, the flatter the trajectory.%1%1Understanding the ballistics of your weapon is the key for precision shooting at longer distances.
STR_A3_BulletDropCompensator2: Bullet Drop Compensators indicate the point of impact at given distances. Some scopes, like the DMS, also have a simple rangefinder (based on the average height of a human standing up-right) to help the shooter measure the distance to the target more precisely.
STR_A3_WeaponResting2: You can stabilize your weapon sway and lower your recoil when you rest your weapon on any surface like a wall or a window frame.%1%1This process is automatic and doesn't require any user input.
STR_A3_WeaponDeployment2: Bipods stabilize your weapon, by reducing sway and recoil, at the cost of reduced mobility.%1%2To deploy your bipod press %11
STR_A3_WeaponDeployment3: You will pivot around your weapon when deployed, allowing you to adjust your view without having to redeploy.
STR_A3_Flashlight2: Flashlights can be mounted on the rails belonging to certain weapons. They help shooters during night operations if they lack night vision. On the other hand, they also give away the shooter's position.%1%2To activate the flashlight, press %11
STR_A3_LaserPointer2: Laser pointers can be attached to certain weapons' side rails. When activated by %11, the laser can be seen via night vision and indicates the exact position that the weapon's barrel is pointing at.%1%1However, if the enemy is also equipped with night vision, the laser may give away the position of the shooter.
STR_A3_MilDot2: Mil-Dot reticles use mathematics to measure distances. To use them properly, you need to: %1%2Know your target's height and/or width %1%2Divide the size (in meters) by the number of mil-dots it takes up in the reticle %1%2Multiply by 1000 to get the distance
STR_A3_MilDot3: Example: enemy tank exposing its side (approx. 8m), taking 10 mils in the scope. 8/10 = 0.8, 0.8*1000 = 800. The tank is 800m away.
STR_A3_Optics2: Weapon sights help you to aim and fire accurately at distant targets.%1%2Press %11 to bring up your optics%1%2Some optics also have alternate sights for shorter ranges. Use %12 to switch between them %1%2Long-range scopes feature variable zoom levels. Use %13 and %14 to zoom in and out %1%2If the zeroing of the optics is not fixed, you can adjust it with %15/%16 to keep your targets in the middle of the crosshair
STR_A3_RemoteCameras2: Remote designators are portable devices used for reconnaissance, target marking, and maintaining the security of strategic areas or objects. Their handling and assembly is similar to the UAVs.%1%2Use %11 and %12 to raise and lower the designator.
STR_A3_Suppression2: One doesn't always have to hit the target to succeed. Bullets flying or impacting around a unit affect its ability to aim, shoot and move. Fire persistently in short intervals to degrade a target's ability to return fire accurately, or deny free movement through certain areas by firing upon them.
STR_A3_Suppression3: With its large magazine capacity and automatic fire mode a machinegun is the weapon of choice for suppressive fire.
str_a3_cfgweapons_srifle_dmr_06_camo_f_l: The Mk14 is a classic battle rifle used in service since the sixties. It is a selective fire automatic rifle that fires the 7.62x51 mm NATO ammunition. Mk14 was replaced by advanced modern variants like Mk18 ABR, but thanks to its low cost, simple construction, and reliability, it is still used in several countries. Civilian hunters in many corners of the world use a single fire version with classic walnut finish, often loaded with a smaller 10 round magazine.
str_a3_cfgweapons_srifle_dmr_05_blk_f_li: Thanks to the 9.3x64 mm ammunition, Cyrus offers better performance than standard 7.62 marksman rifles. At the same time, it is lighter and more versatile than heavy sniper rifles. Cyrus is a gas operated action rifle with single and full auto fire modes. It is a very precise and deadly weapon at a medium distance.
str_a3_cfgweapons_srifle_dmr_04_f_librar: The ASP-1 Kir is a special purpose weapon. This semi-automatic rifle is unique thanks to the built-in silencer and ammunition it uses. The special 12.7x54 mm subsonic round can penetrate heavy body armor at 100 m. Kir is a devastating weapon at short ranges but above 200 m it very quickly loses efficiency.
str_a3_cfgweapons_srifle_dmr_03_f_librar: The Mk-I EMR (Enhanced Marksman Rifle) is a modern marksman rifle chambered in 7.62 mm NATO. It is a light, reliable, and easily serviceable weapon, which can benefit from various attachments. The EMR offers single and full auto fire modes and it is most suited to ranges from 600 to 800 m.
str_a3_cfgweapons_srifle_dmr_02_f_librar: The MAR-10 is a powerful marksman weapon used by CTRG forces. This semi-automatic rifle is chambered in .338 Lapua Magnum. With its 66 cm long barrel and 4.4 kg weight, MAR-10 isn't easy to handle, but high power and extreme precision with effective range up to 1700 m compensate it.
str_a3_cfgweapons_mmg_02_camo_f_library0: The SPMG (Special Purpose Machine Gun) is a lightweight medium machine gun, which greatly benefits from modern materials. It is designed to fill the gap between 7.62 mm and .50 machine guns. The SPMG uses .338 Norma Magnum bullets. The effective range of the machine gun is 1500 m, and thanks to advanced technology, it has a low recoil.
str_a3_cfgweapons_mmg_01_hex_f_library0: Navid is a medium machine gun serving as a powerful support weapon. It uses the 9.3x64 mm ammunition. Navid's weight over 12 kg makes it quite difficult to fire from the standing position, but when deployed, it is a precise and deadly machine gun with outstanding suppressive effect.

str_a3_endgame_tips:
Establish FOB
* Establishing your FOB first will give you an advantage against the enemy forces
* Vehicles respawn at the FOB when destroyed

Download Intel
* Plan to approach Download Intel objectives carefully but quickly, or the enemy might get there first, destroy the Intel, and you won't be able to download
* After downloading Intel from an objective, try to destroy to prevent the opposing side from downloading it themselves
* Use the Dynamic Groups (Press U) to split in teams, and cover multiple objectives at the same time

Secure Schematics
* If your team needs to prevent the opposing team from uploading the schematics make sure to set up good defenses at the enemy upload site
* Hunting the carrier can be a good approach, but remember not to leave the enemy's upload site unprotected
* If your team needs to upload the schematics, make sure to protect the Carrier at all times, the success of the operation is in his hands

Carrier
* When carrying the schematics, if you are on the open, you are visible to the enemy
* Try to move through buildings, trees and other structures so the enemy is not able to pinpoint your current location
* Friendly forces are always able to track the carrier's location

str_a3_endgame_rules:
Both sides must complete three main phases: Establish FOB / Download Intel / Secure Schematics

Establish FOB
* Each playable side must assault and secure their FOB before being able to proceed to the next phase of the operation

Download Intel
* Each side must advance through enemy territory and retrieve useful intel
* The team that downloads enough intel faster will have an advantage for the next phase

Secure Schematics
* There is always one leading and one losing team when the final phase starts
* The leading team must locate and collect the schematics from an unknown location
* The losing team must prevent the opposing team from uploading the schematics
* The losing team can kill the schematics carrier, forcing them to be dropped, which can then be picked up by any player - at this point no team is considered to be leading nor losing
* Taking the schematics and successfully uploading them will determine who wins

STR_A3_Showcase_SlingLoading_Briefing_Si:
We have successfully carried out phase two of our three-phase assault against joint AAF-CSAT forces stationed on Altis. The AAF have been split in two, with entire companies pulling back far to the north-east and south-east ends of the island. CSAT forces, on the other hand, seem to have disappeared entirely.

However, logistics continue to present an obstacle. With phase two culminating in the seizure of the main airbase, along with several surrounding Forward Operating Bases (FOBs), we stand prepared to overcome this obstacle.
STR_A3_Showcase_SlingLoading_Briefing_Mi:
One of our self-propelled artillery platoons, positioned on the eastern coast of the Gulf of Pyrgos, has requested resupply. Your task is to transport ammunition from %2the AAC airfield%1 to their position.

Note: to compensate for the added weight of sling-loaded cargo, your fuel reserve has been limited. Should you require refueling, support forces stationed at %3the AAC airfield%1 are on standby.

2. Collect the ammunition from %2the AAC airfield%1.
3. Transport the ammunition to the %3artillery platoon%1.
4. Return to %4FOB Whiskey%1 and land.

STR_A3_TIME_TRIALS_DIARY_REC5_TEXT:
There are several special Check Point features: timeouts, on-ground requirements and omni-directionality.

Timeouts require you to keep your vehicle within the Check Point area until the timer runs out. This could be to force a hover or landing.

Normal Check Points require you to fly through them from the front to the back. Some Check Points don't have this requirement and can be entered and exited from any direction.

Some Check Points require you to be on the ground (landed). Note that you don't necessarily need to be standing still!
STR_A3_TIME_TRIALS_DIARY_REC6_TEXT:
In some Time Trials you will be asked to sling load objects from one Check Point to another.

When arriving to such Check Point, you will be instructed to pick up the object.

Check Points between the pick-up and drop-off require you to still be carrying the object.

At the drop-off you can earn a bonus for dropping the object as close to the center of the Check Point as possible. A penalty is incurred for damage to the object.
str_a3_time_trials_sp_tt10_overview: A kart has broken down during a race at the Negades Speedway. Bring it back to base and junk another vehicle.
STR_A3_TIME_TRIALS_DIARY_REC7_TEXT:
%1Consider flying Helicopter Time Trials using the Advanced Flight Model available in the game's options. You may shave off a few extra seconds.

%1In helicopters especially, don't fly directly towards a Check Point. Plan your path, anticipate the orientation of the next Check Point and line up in advance.

%1You will not be able to always fly your helicopter at maximum speed. Take inertia into account, burn off excess speed in time and please, mind the ground!
str_a3_time_trials_sp_tt09_overview: This special trial combines several special Check Points, where you need to hover or even land.
str_a3_time_trials_sp_tt08_overview: In this trial your helicopter handling is put to the ultimate test. Complete tight turns, survive rapid descents and manage your RPMs well.
STR_A3_TIME_TRIALS_END6_DESC: You've damaged the cargo too much.
str_a3_time_trials_sp_tt07_overview: With its spaced out Check Points across the Altian countryside, this trial blends high speeds and terrain following abilities. Watch out for wind turbines and power lines!
str_a3_time_trials_sp_tt06_overview: This introductory helicopter trial consists of a simple loop around the airport's runways and taxiways.
STR_A3_TIME_TRIALS_HELI_OVERVIEW: Fly helicopters through an increasingly challenging series of aerial courses. Split-second decisions, engine performance management and aerobatic maneuvers demand excellent piloting skills.
str_a3_time_trials_hint_rules1a: Wait or gain some speed to quick-start!

STR_A3_MP_GS_SC_01_Briefing_Situation_te: After their failed invasion of Altis, NATO forces are consolidating their forces around the AAC airfield and Poliakko. CSAT, on the other hand, have reinforced their positions at Neochori and are preparing to launch a major counterattack in the hope of driving NATO forces from Altis.
STR_A3_MP_GS_SC_01_Overview_text: Invading NATO forces defend themselves from a CSAT counterattack.
STR_A3_MP_GS_SC_02_Briefing_Situation_te: Having successfully routed the AAF, forcing them to retreat to the north-east and south-east corners of Altis, NATO forces prepare to deliver the final blow. However, the AAF are far from defeated. As NATO prepare to launch their assault from Delfinaki, the AAF are consolidating their forces around Molos in the hope of stopping NATO in their tracks.
STR_A3_MP_GS_SC_02_Overview_text: Retreating AAF defend themselves from a NATO offensive.
STR_A3_MP_GS_SC_03_Briefing_Situation_te: For reasons that are, as of yet, unclear, AAF and CSAT forces have declared an immediate dissolution of their alliance and a commencement of hostilities. The capital of Altis, Pyrgos, remains a no-man's land, holding immense value to both sides. The AAF prepare to launch their assault from the north, while CSAT intend to counter from the south.
STR_A3_MP_GS_SC_03_Overview_text: CSAT-AAF relations have disintegrated. Both sides prepare to stake it all on Pyrgos, the capital.
STR_A3_MP_GS_COOP_01_Briefing_Situation_: Labelled an insurgency by the local government, the FIA have reveled in a string of victories against the AAF, seizing major ground in the process. The AAF have called upon CSAT for assistance. In response, elements of one of CSAT's elite Airborne Battalions have been deployed to the region to launch counter-insurgency operations against the FIA.
STR_A3_MP_GS_COOP_01_Overview_text: Members of an elite CSAT Airborne Battalion launch an offensive against the FIA.
STR_A3_MP_GS_COOP_02_Briefing_Situation_: Months after Task Force Aegis went dark, the 111th Division have successfully commenced their invasion of Stratis with the capture of the Stratis Air Base. However, the rest of the island remains under AAF control, with defenses strategically positioned at all major installations. As a result, the 111th are coming at them from the north-west, supported by the FIA from the south, with the intention of catching the AAF off-guard.
STR_A3_MP_GS_COOP_02_Overview_text: The 111th Division launch their invasion of Stratis.

str_a3_mp_groundsupport_hints_cas_reques: A Close-Air-Support request was registered and a new task was added. To complete the task, destroy the enemy vehicle marked by the waypoint.
This is a high priority task as the vehicle can decimate several units if it's not quickly dispatched. This task has the highest Score reward.
str_a3_mp_groundsupport_hints_crash_land: You have survived, but your helicopter is out of action. Because you were not killed in the crash, you do not receive the score penalty for dying. As a bonus, your respawn time has also been decreased.
str_a3_mp_groundsupport_hints_group_mark:
By pressing %11 you can toggle group markers on friendly units. The group markers consist of several elements:
%2 middle - unit type.
%2 left - request type.
%2 right - selected by player.
str_a3_mp_groundsupport_hints_medevac_re: A medevac request was registered and a new task was added. To complete the task, land close to the group leader and wait until the group gets in. Afterwards, transport the group to the medevac area at base.
This is a medium priority task as the successful extraction of the affected group will free up the used Manpower by them, and allow another fresh group to join the battle.
str_a3_mp_groundsupport_hints_resupply_r: A resupply request was registered and a new task was added. To complete the task, sling load an ammo create stored at the maintenance area at the base and drop it close to the requested group leader.
This is a medium priority task as soldiers without ammunition will not be effective on the battlefield.
str_a3_mp_groundsupport_hints_score_incr: Your %3Score%4 was just increased as a reward for completing a task, and you have directly contributed to your side's next %3Tactical Strike%4.
Check the %3Tips%4 section for more information about %3Score%4 and %3Tactical Strikes%4.
str_a3_mp_groundsupport_hints_tactical_s: Well done! A %3Tactical Strike%4 was just initiated by Headquarters.
The approximate location of the %3Tactical Strike% is marked on the map.
str_a3_mp_groundsupport_hints_transport_: A transport request was registered and a new task was added. To complete the task, land close to the group leader and wait until the group gets in. Afterwards, transport the group to the designated sector (marked by the waypoint) %3OR%4 any other sector that is not under our control.
This is the most common task. It has lower priority then the other tasks as the units can reach their destinations unassisted. Although, transport logistics can be of high tactical significance.
str_a3_mp_groundsupport_tips_completingt: There are 4 type of tasks, sorted by their strategic importance and Score that they reward you with: Close Air Support > Resupply > Medevac > Transport.
STR_A3_SlingLoad2: Sling loading is the process of using ropes to transport extra cargo underneath a helicopter.%1%2Each helicopter has a cargo weight limit, which also needs to be compatible with the hook system.
STR_A3_SlingLoad3: Remember that, with the advanced flight model, the amount of fuel onboard, and the number of people inside the helicopter, are also included in the cargo weight limit.%1The flight characteristics of the helicopter will also change depending on the cargo being sling loaded.
STR_A3_SlingLoadManager2: The Sling Load Assistant is activated with %11. It is used to identify, navigate to, and attach desired objects within the vicinity of the helicopter.%1%1%2The Assistant consists of the following components:%1%2%3Target Indicators%4 - objects that can be attached%1%2%3Altitude Bar%4 - measures the height of the helicopter above the targeted object%1%2%3Crosshairs%4 - indicates whether the helicopter is properly aligned with the targeted object%1%2%3Status Bar%4 - communicates the current status of the helicopter's ropes
str_a3_heliyaw_sub2_desc: While at cruising speed, yawing will be less effective. To turn the helicopter left and right, use %11 and %12, respectively.
str_a3_heliyaw_sub1_desc: If the helicopter is hovering or traveling at low speeds, %1%2use %11 to rotate to the left and%1%2%12 to rotate right.
str_a3_heliyaw_main_tip: As the forward speed of the helicopter increases, pedals become less effective.%1%1%13
str_a3_heliyaw_main_desc: Turning at lower speeds is done via pedal input. Helicopters with one main rotor use pedals to change the thrust produced by the tail rotor, in order to compensate for the amount of torque being produced by the main rotor.%1%1%2To yaw to the left, use %11.%1%2To yaw right, use %12.
STR_A3_VehicleTurrets2: Turrets mounted on vehicles are usually operated by a gunner who can either target and engage enemies independently, or can be assigned a specific target by the vehicle commander or pilot.
str_a3_helivortexring_main_tip: %1In single rotor helicopters, the Vortex Ring State can be corrected by moving the cyclic control forward, which controls the pitch angle of the rotor blade, slightly pitching nose down, and establishing forward flight.
str_a3_helivortexring_main_desc: The Advanced flight model simulates what is known as the Vortex Ring State. Also known as Settling with Power, it is a dangerous phenomenon. Essentially, the helicopter descends into its own downwash. The pilot experiences an increasing sink rate that cannot be stopped by the collective.%1%1In tandem-rotor helicopters, recovery is accomplished through lateral cyclic or pedal input. The aircraft will fly into 'clean air', and will be able to regain lift.
str_a3_helitrim_main_desc: %1The Advanced flight model allows you to trim the controls.%1The so-called Auto-trim feature is a game difficulty option that handles anti-torque pedal input.%1Enabling Manual Trim allows control over the center position offset (incl. pedals). When you have established your new desired flight attitude, you can disable Manual Trim %11 and return controls to neutral position. There are other keys that can be used to adjust each controller offset gradually.
str_a3_helitranslationallift_main_tip: As a result, the helicopter requires less power to keep itself in the air. Lower the collective if you need to maintain the same altitude.%1
str_a3_helitranslationallift_main_desc: As a helicopter moves from hover to forward flight, it enters a state called translational lift. The horizontal flow of air across the main rotor improves its efficiency, which provides extra lift without increasing power.
str_a3_helitailloss_main_desc: Helicopters equipped with a tail rotor can suffer from losing tail anti-tourque authority. In such instances, attempt to land while maintaining sufficient forward speed.
str_a3_helistressdamage_main_desc: The Advanced flight model calculates both the force on the rotors (drag) and the transmission (torque). The pilot can exceed construction limits and break each component. Those limits can be turned off in the game difficulty settings, but forces on rotors will still be simulated and may result in the loss of main rotor RPM. This will cause the helicopter to stall. The pilot must lower the collective %11 in order to recover.
str_a3_heliroll_sub3_desc: To make a sharper turn, pitch the nose up %11 while turning left or right. Keep an eye on your speed!
str_a3_heliroll_sub2_desc: %2To turn left while at cruising speed, use %11.%1%2To turn right, use %12.
str_a3_heliroll_sub1_desc: To move in a strafing fashion, keep the helicopter stationary and %1%2roll left with %11%1%2or roll right with %12.
str_a3_heliroll_main_desc: With the helicopter in a hover, moving the cyclic left or right will cause helicopter to slip sideways. If the helicopter flies at higher speeds it will roll, turning to the left or the right (similar to the behavior of fixed wing aircraft).%1%1%2To roll to the left, push the cyclic left %11.%1%2To roll to the right, push the cyclic right %12.
str_a3_helipitch_sub4_desc: To transition the helicopter into a hover while moving forward, %1%2pitch the nose up %11%1%2 and lower the collective %12%1simultaneously to prevent the helicopter from gaining altitude.
str_a3_helipitch_sub3_tip: %14%1To easily enter a hover, %1use the %3Autohover%4 function %13.
str_a3_helipitch_sub3_desc: Use the cyclic to slow the helicopter down during forward flight.%1%1%2Pitch the nose up %12 or %1%2down %11 as required.
str_a3_helipitch_sub2_desc: To easily enter a hover, %1use the %3Autohover%4 function %11.
str_a3_helipitch_sub1_desc: %2To increase your speed use %11.%1%2To decrease your speed use %12.
str_a3_helipitch_main_tip: %13%1The more cyclic you apply, the more the helicopter will move.
STR_A3_HeliRotation_sub2: %2Use the rudder %11 and %12 to rotate left/right
str_a3_helipitch_main_desc: The cyclic is used to change the pitch of the main rotor blades as they cycle around. This controls the main rotor's direction of thrust, allowing the helicopter to move forwards, backwards or sideways. Note that it will also have an effect on the helicopter's altitude.%1%1%2To pitch down, push the cyclic forwards %11.%1%2To pitch up, pull the cyclic backwards %12.
str_a3_helilandinggear_main_tip: Make sure to retract the landing gear after take-off so it won't affect the aerodynamics of your aircraft.
str_a3_helilandinggear_main_desc: In an aircraft equipped with foldable landing gear:%1%1%2Deploy the gear with %11%1%2Retract the gear with %12
str_a3_heligroundeffect_sub1_desc: Use Autohover %11 to make the helicopter hover on its own.
str_a3_heligroundeffect_main_tip: Normal airflow pattern%1%1%12%1%1For better handling use %3Autohover%4 %11
str_a3_heligroundeffect_main_desc: While hovering your helicopter near the ground (within 1/2 the diameter of the rotor), it will be influenced by ground effect. Ground effect is due to interference of the surface with the airflow pattern of the rotor. The aerodynamics change, requiring the pilot to compensate.
str_a3_helicollective_sub2_desc: To move forward without losing altitude, %1%2pitch the nose down %11 and %1%2raise the collective %12.
str_a3_helicollective_sub1_desc: %2Hold %11 to raise the collective and gain altitude.%1%2Hold %12 to lower the collective and lose altitude.
str_a3_helicollective_main_desc: The collective is used for changing the pitch angle of all the main rotor blades collectively. It controls the amount of thrust provided by the main rotor, increasing or decreasing the amount of lift and the amount of torque. This way the helicopter can ascend or descend.%1%1%2To ascend, raise the collective %11.%1%2Descend by lowering the collective %12.
STR_A3_HeliLanding_sub2: %2Hold %11 to decrease throttle and lose altitude.%1%2Pull the nose up %12 to lose speed.%1%2Use the %3mouse%4 to control the helicopter smoothly
str_a3_heliautorotation_sub1_desc: When experiencing a loss of engine power:%1%1%2Drop the collective %11%1%2Gain sufficient forward speed %12%1%2Maintain a nominal RPM and glide%1%2Before touchdown, raise the collective %13
str_a3_heliautorotation_main_desc: Autorotation is a state of flight where the main rotor system of a helicopter turns only as a result of air moving up through the rotor, as with an auto gyro, rather than engine power driving the rotor. Thanks to this ability, a helicopter can land safely in the event of complete engine failure.%1%1When experiencing a loss of engine power, drop collective with %11. You can also pitch the nose down %12 to gain sufficient forward speed. Maintain a nominal RPM and glide until close to the ground. Raise the collective %13 before touchdown to reduce vertical speed and land safely.
str_a3_cfghints_premiumcontent_premiumhe: Start the engines! Jump into new cargo helicopters and master a new sling loading feature to gain an advantage on the battlefield in the Arma 3 Helicopters DLC.%1%1%2CH-67 Huron - NATO's twin-engine, tandem rotor heavy-lift helicopter%1%2Mi-290 Taru - CSAT heavy utility helicopter using a coaxial rotor design%1%2M-900 - Civilian variant of the existing H-9 family of helicopters%1%2Sling Loading Objects%1%2Helicopter Objects%1%2F.O.B. Objects%1%2Support Multiplayer - a new mode in which battlefield logistics play a major role%1%24 VR Helicopter Training Course%1%2Showcase Sling Loading%1%25 Singleplayer Time Trial Challenges%1%2Set of extra Steam Achievements
STR_A3_AutoHover2: Activating auto-hover will automatically stabilize your aircraft. Note that while auto-hover is active, the controls will have a reduced effect.%1%2Select %3Auto hover%4 from the action menu.%1%2Or quickly press %11 to activate it.
STR_A3_CargoHook2: To attach an object to your helicopter, hover over the object at a low altitude and press %11 to deploy your ropes. Remain stationary until the ropes attach to the object.%1%1%2If you're using the Sling Load Assistant:%1%2Press %11 to deploy your ropes when prompted%1%2Align the %3Target Indicator%4 with the %3Crosshairs%4%1%2Maintain the desired altitude indicated by the %3Altitude Bar%4%1%2Remain stationary as the %3Status Bar%4 fills until the object is successfully attached
STR_A3_CargoHook3: Remember that the ropes can break if too much force is exerted on the cargo itself, e.g. hitting an obstacle or having the helicopter pefrom a more-violent maneuver.
STR_A3_CargoUnhook2: To safely detach cargo, hover above the drop zone and slowly decrease your altitude.%1%2Don't forget to include the height of your cargo and the length of the rope(s) to your calculations.%1%2Detach the cargo with %11.
STR_A3_CargoUnhook3: In case of emergency, you can also detach the cargo mid-flight. If it isn't destroyed upon impact, you may be able to hook it up again later.
STR_A3_CFGVEHICLES_B_HELI_LIGHT_01_ARMOR: A light single-engine helicopter used in special operations by the US Army since the Vietnam War. It now exists in several variants used by both military and civilian transport. The AH-9 Pawnee variant is a light helicopter with the ability to carry anti-ground fixed forward-firing weapons such as unguided rockets and machine guns to provide direct air-support for the special operations forces. The MH-9 Hummingbird is mostly used as a special forces troop transport with two outboard benches. The M-900 is a civilian version. Closed cabin and comfortable interior provides space for two passengers.
STR_A3_FieldManualLink: Some hints point to entries in the %3Field Manual%4. There, you will find more detailed information on the topic. %1%2Open the map by pressing %11.%1%2Select the Log tab from the list on the left.%1%2Select the Hints tab from the list that appears.%1%2Click the topic you want know more about.%1You will then be taken to the associated entry in the Field Manual.
STR_A3_FieldManualLinkTip: Hints that have been shown in the current session are highlited in the Field Manual by
STR_A3_TimeTrials_HelicopterCPs1: There are several special Check Point features: timeouts, on-ground requirements and omni-directionality.
STR_A3_TimeTrials_HelicopterCPs2: Timeouts require you to keep your vehicle within the Check Point area until the timer runs out. This could be to force a hover or landing.%1%1Normal Check Points require you to fly through them from the front to the back. Some Check Points don't have this requirement and can be entered and exited from any direction.%1%1Some Check Points require you to be on the ground (landed). Note that you don't necessarily need to be standing still!
STR_A3_TimeTrials_SL1: In some Time Trials you will be asked to sling load objects from one Check Point to another.
STR_A3_TimeTrials_SL2: When arriving at such a Check Point, you will be instructed to pick up the object.%1%1Check Points between the pick-up and drop-off require you to still be carrying the object.%1%1At the drop-off you can earn a bonus for dropping the object as close to the center of the Check Point as possible. A penalty is incurred for damage to the object.
STR_A3_HeliFlight_sub2: %2Pull the nose down %11 to gain speed and up %12 to lose it%1%2Hold %13 to increase throttle and gain altitude%1%2Hold %14 to decrease throttle and lose altitude%1%2Maneuver the helicopter sideways with %15 and %16%1%2Use the rudder %17 and %18 to rotate left/right%1%2Use the %3mouse%4 to control the helicopter smoothly
STR_A3_HeliAdvancedFM_main_desc: An alternative Flight Dynamics Model is optionally available for all official helicopters. It provides a more authentic rotary-wing experience and offers precise control over helicopters.
STR_A3_HeliAdvancedFM_main_tip: The Advanced Flight Model can be toggled on or off at any time in the Game Options. You can also configure several simulation helpers there. Certain scenarios may force one or the other Flight Model for all players.
STR_A3_TimeTrials_HelicopterTips1: Consider flying Helicopter Time Trials using the Advanced Flight Model available in the game's options. You may shave off a few extra seconds.
STR_A3_TimeTrials_HelicopterTips2: In helicopters especially, don't fly directly towards a Check Point. Plan your path, anticipate the orientation of the next Check Point and line up in advance.%1%1You will not be able to always fly your helicopter at maximum speed. Take inertia into account, burn off excess speed in time and please, mind the ground!
STR_A3_HeliAerialCombat_desc: There are several ways to avoid being hit by enemies:%1%1%2Higher altitudes give you an advantage over them%1%2Maintaining high speed will make it difficult for them to track you
STR_A3_HeliAltitude_sub2: %2Hold %11 to increase throttle and gain altitude%1%2Hold %12 to decrease throttle and lose altitude
STR_A3_HeliAutorotation_sub1_tip: To increase the RPM of the main rotor, pitch the nose above the horizon while keeping the collective lowered.
STR_A3_helilookdown_main_desc: The cockpit often restricts the view of the pilot, making it difficult to land safely.%1To improve the view from the cockpit, activate Freelook using %11. %1%2You can also look down using %12.%1%2Alternatively, you can look up using %13.%1%2To recenter your view, use %14.
STR_A3_helivelocityvector_main_desc: To better predict the movement of the helicopter, make use of the HUD's %3Velocity Vector indicator%4 visible from the cockpit. %1%2The indicator tells you where the helicopter is actually moving. %3Try to line it up with your destination.%4
STR_A3_helivelocityvector_main_hint: Align the indicator with the helipad you intend to land at.
STR_A3_TARU_DESC_F0: The Mi-290 Taru is a CSAT heavy utility helicopter with coaxial rotors and a unique modular construction. Its design is inspired by both Kamov Ka-226 and S-64 Skycrane aircraft. Various mission pods allow Taru to serve many different roles. Primarily it can transport cargo (up to 13,500 kg), troops (up to 16 passengers), and provide battlefield supplies (ammunition, fuel, repair facilities, and medical equipment). The helicopter can also transport light vehicles thanks to Sling Loading capabilities. While the Taru is unarmed, it does have countermeasure launchers.
STR_A3_HURON_DESC_F0: The CH-67 Huron is a twin-engine, tandem rotor heavy-lift helicopter used by NATO. Its primary role is the transportation of troops, vehicles and cargo. The maximum weight of cargo it's able to lift is 12 tons. The Huron is a modernized version of the CH-47 Chinook and exists in two variants. The armed variant with two side gunners manning 6.5 mm Miniguns offers some defensive capabilities, while the transport version replaces the gunners with additional two passengers positions.
STR_A3_M900_DESC_F0: A light single-engine helicopter used in special operations by the US Army since the Vietnam War. It now exists in several variants used by both military and civilian transport. The M-900 is a civilian version. Closed cabin and comfortable interior provides space for two passengers.
STR_A3_SlingLoadManager3: Some transport helicopters are equipped with a downward facing camera to help the pilot with the precision navigation of the cargo. To enter the camera, use %11.

str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_heli_pard: Arma 3 Helicopters arrives with the following premium content and platform additions:
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_heli_parc_list4: Various helicopter tweaks improve the experience of flight: manual landing gear operation, G-force camera shake, enhanced sound effects and more.
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_heli_parc_list3: Use your personal weapons from specific passenger positions in a wide range of vehicles.

str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_heli_parc: Our approach is that new gameplay features are available to everyone who owns Arma 3. We've selected features that complement the premium content and vice versa. Based on some of the top-voted requests, we think you'll like these improvements to the sandbox:
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_heli_parb: Arma 3 Helicopters is a content pack. With our Karts testing DLC, we introduced a strategy for premium content. Based on your feedback and results from our survey, we've iterated the 'try before you buy' approach and will continue to do so. Owners get full access to 2 brand-new detailed rotary-wing aircraft: the CH-67 Huron, Mi-290 Taru, and their variants. These helicopters were selected and designed to fulfill an important logistical role on the battlefield. Combined with new features, they can carry more troops than previous aircraft as well as carry more cargo. A range of official playable modes demonstrates the helicopters and generally focuses on aerial movement, combat and logistics.
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_heli_para: Greetings rotorheads! The <t color='%1'>Arma 3 Helicopters</t> DLC has been released, bringing cool new content for DLC owners, while also enriching the Arma 3 sandbox for everyone else. Take a look below at what assets we've added and the huge features that were implemented, or just give it a whirl right here, right now!

str_a3_time_trials_diary_rec1_text:
Time Trials are a series of vehicle-based races against the clock.

Competitors navigate a string of Check Points in order to reach the finish line as quickly as possible.

They refine their skills in the areas of vehicle handling, cornering, navigation, memorization and split-second decision-making.
str_a3_time_trials_diary_rec2_text:
A competitor's raw time is the amount of time it takes to reach the final Check Point.

Time may be added when you are penalized, for missing a Check Point for example.

Competitors compete for medals: beat the bronze, silver and gold times. Sometimes a special time is available.
str_a3_time_trials_diary_rec3_text:
You will need to move through all Check Points in a trial for the best possible time.

However, you are allowed to miss Check Points at the cost of a time penalty.

Memorize the trial by training often. Some trials support immediate looping when you cross the start right after the final Check Point.
str_a3_time_trials_diary_rec4_text:
%1Time Trials are not intended to be mastered in one attempt. Study the trials, find shortcuts and repeat them often.

%1Sometimes it is better to accept missing a Check Point, taking the penalty, and moving on.

%1You can disable the on-screen Check Point indicators via difficulty flag 'HUD waypoints info'.

str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_malden_pard: Arma 3 Malden DLC contains the following free content for everyone who owns the base game:
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_malden_parc: To (re)introduce Malden to you in a fun way, we are releasing a completely new multiplayer mode, Combat Patrol, as well as instances of the Escape mode for our two most recent terrains (Tanoa and Malden). Combat Patrol is a quick and dynamic cooperative multiplayer mode in which you are a member of an infantry team with the possibility to select the Area of Operations. Each play-through will be different thanks to the mode's heavily randomized nature and behavior. If you want to experience authentic Arma gameplay, then Combat Patrol is a great starting point. The mode is available for all of our official terrains, including Malden. Escape is the multiplayer mode known from its original Altis variant, now also available for Malden and Tanoa (as a bonus for Apex owners). Can you handle the challenge and escape the islands together against overwhelming odds?
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_malden_parb: Malden 2035 is our fresh take on the original Malden. We've tried to stay as close as possible to the vision of the original island and hopefully veterans of the series will find lots of familiar places. While Malden re-uses many vanilla Arma 3 structures, vegetation, and similar assets, we have also included some splendid additions such as colored buildings, vineyards, and barns. These have helped us to recreate the terrain to Arma 3 standards. Malden benefits from Argo's infantry focus, where a lot of effort was put into the gameplay flow of each location. As such, Malden is more suitable for Close Quarters Combat than previous terrains. Now go and explore the desert, rocky cliffs, dense forests and other impressive areas!
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_malden_para: Welcome back to Malden, soldier! Sixteen years ago, we started our amazing journey with the Arma franchise here. We hope you'll enjoy this recreation of <t color='%1'>Malden</t>, which is sure to bring back many memories of a certain flashpoint occurring on the island. Alongside the new terrain, we are also releasing a new cooperative mode: <t color='%1'>Combat Patrol</t>. Please enjoy this free DLC as a token of our appreciation to the best community in the world. You have been with us every step of the way and got Arma to where it is now. <t color='%1'>Thank you!</t>
str_a3_cfghints_maldendlc_maldenterrain1: %1Visit the terrain where we first embarked on our journey of the Arma franchise. Malden 2035 is not just a one-to-one recreation of the classic Malden in Arma: Cold War Assault. It offers a fresh take on the surroundings we know and love, with new locations to find and explore, such as the Arma: Mobile Ops Base or Radio Tower. While Malden re-uses many vanilla Arma 3 structures, vegetation, and similar assets, we have also made some splendid additions such as colored houses, vineyards and farm buildings. We hope you will enjoy this new re-imagination of Malden. May it bring back many of your fondest Arma memories! %1%1%3OVERVIEW%4% %1%2 Size - 62 km2 of land mass %1%2 Varied locations - deserts, forests, farmlands, towns, and more %1%2 Structures - colored houses, vineyards, barns, and more %1%2 Signs - new directional signs, bus stops, and community-made billboards
str_a3_cfghints_maldendlc_malden1: %1Everyone is invited to celebrate the 16th Armaversary on a modern re-imagination of the classic Malden terrain. Dive into the authentic and dynamic Combat Patrol multiplayer mode and complete tactical objectives on all vanilla terrains. This DLC is free for all players as token of appreciation to the best community in the world. %1%1%3DLC CONTENTS%4 %1%2 Malden 2035 %1%2 New / refreshed structures and objects %1%2 Combat Patrol %1%2 Escape from Malden / Tanoa %1%2 Orchestral Theme Song %1More about Arma 3 Malden
str_a3_cfghints_maldendlc_combatpatrol1: %1A new, quick and dynamic cooperative multiplayer mode has been made available for all our vanilla terrains, including Malden 2035. Search an Area of Operations of your choosing, complete assigned objectives and ex-filtrate in one piece. You can accomplish your mission quietly or eliminate all hostiles in a coordinated shock assault; your team decides on the best approach. Be on your guard however, the mode randomizes several aspects for every attempt. Combat Patrol is a great starting point to experience authentic Arma gameplay together!

str_a3_showcase_future_diary_situation_d:
On paper, this conflict's over - a ceasefire's been called and hostilities have stopped across the island.

The reality on the ground however, is somewhat different. In the northern town of Sofia, non-state actors from the Freedom and Independence Army have cornered a rag-tag group of Altis Armed Forces. Most are looking to throw in the towel, but others are intent on continuing the fight. Indeed, we suspect that some of these die-hard combatants are war criminals, so don't expect them to go quietly. In addition, we've received reports of widespread looting. It's important that we act now. Cultural property is under threat, and we have a legal obligation to protect it.

str_a3_showcase_future_diary_mission_des: Your special operations team will enter the AO by helicopter and insert south of Sofia, before meeting local friendly forces at Point Charlie. Here you will gather important intel on the situation and assist in removing any hostile forces from the town. Support units from Alpha and Bravo will arrive by air and join the operation from the north, rounding-up any surrendering AAF combatants. Once we’re in control of Sofia, you will work with Captain Hepworth of the British Cultural Rescue Initiative to secure a precious artwork in accordance with the Laws of Armed Conflict. Similarly, you will uphold the Rules of Engagement, avoiding collateral damage and returning fire only if attacked.
str_a3_showcase_future_letter:
To my enemy,

You are close and therefore, my time is short.
To my family, I have said all that can be said. To you, there is still the truth. That was our first casualty - and yours. It has condemned me and now, it shall avenge me, for we did not start this war.
You did. You coordinated the terrorist attack on Stratis and you murdered my countrymen. The evidence is here. All of it. Irrefutable evidence. But then, perhaps we have both been deceived. Perhaps we are not even enemies at all.
I am sorry for what's become of my country. Nothing else. I gave consent to greater nations to save our own, to shake the earth with Poseidon's wrath and level the world.

Forgive me.

str_a3_showcase_aow_titlecard_showcase_t: SHOWCASE: ART OF WAR - Community Artwork, Gallery Exhibition, IHL in Future Conflict
str_a3_showcase_aow_mission_desc: Step inside the Lars Blanken Gallery and discover an exhibition on the art of war.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_winged_infantr:
David Mustache
Winged Infantry

The striking sense of movement in this picture is astounding. It demonstrates both obvious technical ability and a careful eye for composition. The consistent and earthly palette of pale and dark greens, present in the parachutes, uniforms, grass, and distant trees also add a stunning conformity and emphasize the idea of many individual parts working as a whole; a true artistic, combined arms operation.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_translating:
Professor Death
Translating

Small quadcopter drones have played an important role in enforcing International Humanitarian Law in recent years. In this picture, we can see an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) belonging to the Canton Protocol Strategic Alliance Treaty, observing the processing of prisoners. Through remote surveillance, combatants on all sides are under increasing pressure to comply with the rules of war.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_think_again:
Laurentius Kus Savata Reyhan
Think Again

This poster with its didactic question masks a sophisticated artistic conceit. By overlapping and combining the profiles of several autonomous weapon systems, we are encouraged to separate their forms and exercise our sensory perception; just as a machine is expected to distinguish potential threats from non-combatants or cultural property. If we, as humans, struggle to depict these components, is it too much to expect from robots?
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_the_road_ahead:
EO
The Road Ahead

This multivalent work, with its overcast skies and gloomy atmosphere, carries an almost dream-like quality. The solitary drone, approaching an urban environment obscured by fog, hints at a journey into the unknown and evokes the idea of technology on a road towards an uncertain future. And who is in control? A human operator? Or is this vehicle fully autonomous, and rolling forwards on its own initiative?
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_the_patrol:
William Thomas Nuckolls
The Patrol

A soldier relies upon their senses to make correct decisions on the battlefield. But as this curious painting shows, accurate observation is not always easy. Here, we can vaguely make out the silhouettes of soldiers moving through a field, partially obscured by their environment and its twilight shadows. Although it's clear there are combatants present, are all of them legitimate targets?
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_the_giftgivers:
Maria Isabel Rauber Neves Martinewski
The Gift-Givers
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_the_extraction:
Greenfist
The Extraction

As military technologies become increasingly sophisticated and climate change fuels competition for resources, it is not altogether surprising that more of the world has become prone to conflict. The melting arctic circle, in particular, has become a contested arena of major strategic importance.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_technomachy:
Stelios Afentakis
Technomachy

Although it might appear like science fiction, this busy combat scene presages an authentic glimpse of tomorrow’s battlefields. Urban environments, swarming with ground and aerial combat drones, autonomous medical units, and soldiers, clad in dehumanizing armor, strike us now as a grounded interpretation of what is to come. The legal and humanitarian challenges these new forms of warfare present are a pressing global concern.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_tango_down:
Austin Spears
Tango Down

This screenshot from a military simulation game raises some important questions regarding the fetishization of violence in popular culture. Are we becoming desensitized to representations of conflict? Or are video games and other interactive media a lens for exploring real-world concerns and unpleasant realities, challenging preconceptions and perspectives? Do the developers of these products have moral obligations in how they portray modern conflict? Or are they simply expected to create? And can video games be considered art at all? This last point, remains divisive.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_tactical_withd:
Austin McGinty
Tactical Withdrawal

The cluster of menacing robotic soldiers in this work, standing against the bright orange glow of a featureless city aflame, are in fact, allowing enemy combatants to pull a wounded comrade to safety. Are these faceless entities observing the spirit of International Humanitarian Law? Do they suggest a coming era of restraint in modern warfare, free of human folly and passions? Or is this simply indifference? A short, calculating pause before an algorithm loads and the systematic killing continues? Like the future itself, this piece presents us with a vision that is difficult to decipher.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_sentries:
Joseph Braden Banks
Sentries

This beautifully composed image, showing a group of sentries standing guard, highlights a reality of war that is seldom the subject of great works of art; waiting. Indeed, today, many soldiers never see action. This restrained work eschews romanticized notions of the battlefield and instead, presents a more grounded and nuanced snapshot of modern conflict, as experienced by the majority of military personnel.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_robogeddon:
Greenfist
Robogeddon

Although seemingly absurd, this vision of the future is fast becoming a very plausible and very concerning reality. After the Quantum Revolution of the late 2020's, we are now faced with highly intelligent thinking machines, wired for war, interconnected, and supposedly subservient to the highest echelons of power. But what happens when the first robots become self-aware - when ascendance becomes transcendence? This possibility is causing great consternation amongst leading scientists and academics today, who fear tomorrow's war won't be one fought between humans.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_remote_respons:
Maria Komarova & Diana Pomortseva
Remote Response

In the past, logistics were a serious challenge for humanitarian organizations. But today, modern technology has helped us transcend many practical problems. From robotic pack mules, able to traverse the most inhospitable mountain ranges, to squadrons of utility drones, capable of transporting life-saving aid to populations under siege, many things have changed for the better.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_reassessment:
Kiko Mazar
Reassessment

The sharp contrasts, post-processing effects, and angular shadows that dissect this scene perfectly echo the intensity of the chaotic situation, as experienced by the soldiers. Each combatant crouches behind cover and seemingly melds with their environment, as if swallowed by the hostile surroundings. The enemy is nowhere to be seen. However, the non-presence is a presence in itself and brilliantly communicates feelings of unease and tension. The photograph also addresses an increasing trend in modern conflict; the urbanization of the battlefield. Consequently, it seems both familiar and contemporary.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_one_of_many:
Diego Ferreirós González
One of Many

Like the rows of military graves in cemeteries across the world, this sober image highlights the human cost of conflict in no uncertain terms. In the context of modern warfare, it also poses some difficult questions. Not only in relation to reasons for war but with regards to the methods of waging it. Are autonomous weapons, for instance, an opportunity to save soldiers' lives? Do we really want to remove these tragic consequences, allowing nations to project force with impunity? And how can we argue against robots on the battlefield with the loved ones of combatants who have made an ultimate, yet ultimately avoidable sacrifice? Perhaps, scenes like this one, are a necessary reality of war?
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_moving_up:
Descryver ‘Papa Bear’ Stéphane
Moving Up

In this picture, medics treat wounded combatants while soldiers from the US 5th Army file by, temporarily united, both in service and in the sacrifices demanded of them. It's a poignant scene, where the serenity and stillness of the Italian landscape is cleverly juxtaposed against the movement of infantry and tanks - a beautiful intermezzo in what could be called a symphony of war.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_man_with_child:
Pedro Augusto Guerreiro Rodrigues
Man with Child

This touching photograph is a powerful reminder of how armed conflict can impact children. Aside from the nightmarish imagery, embodied here by faceless soldiers in hazmat suits, war causes intense psychological trauma through the severance of emotional and physical ties. The experiences of young victims, forced to abandon homes and loved ones, often transcend generations and inflict indiscernible wounds, many of which remain for life.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_lockdown:
Pedro Augusto Guerreiro Rodrigues
Lockdown

As this photograph from Chernarus during the 2020 pandemic shows, humankind has known many forms of conflict. Frequently described as 'a fight' against an 'invisible enemy', lockdown measures were often permeated by the language of war, indicating the latter's close connection to the human condition and its importance as a common framework of understanding. Should then, war art encompass 'wars' against poverty, crime, class and climate change? How can we define 'war'? By its dictionary definition, or by how we perceive it?
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_little_green_m:
Yooles
Little Green Men

This powerful photograph, originally published in the News Today, neatly captures the changing nature of modern conflict. The old maxim that truth is the first casualty of war seems to be symptomatic of our times. Modern technology has introduced us to an age of subjective realities. But can this same technology resolve the problems it has created? Or must we rely upon our own discretion to sort facts from fiction?
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_lars_blanken:
Unknown Artist
Lars Blanken

Portrait of the Dutch philanthropist and founder of the International Development & Aid Project, Lars Blanken. The wealthy son of a shipbuilding tycoon and war profiteer, Blanken turned his back on the pursuit of profit and became an instrumental figure in the Refugee Council, based in Leiden, supporting the Belgian diaspora through the First World War. This gallery is named in his honor. Visitors may notice the inscription on the fresco around the glass rotunda. It is a reference to Blanken's famous quote: 'Gentlemen, man's humanity has been weighed and found wanting - but together we can tip the scales.'
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_gray_goo:
Otto Petäjä
'Gray Goo'

In this famous work of abstract art, we are offered a chillingly prophetic vision of future conflict. Simply entitled 'Gray Goo', it alludes to the gray, slime-like appearance of molecular nanotechnology. Once a hypothetical concept, it became the controversial subject of military study in 2033. Today, propelled by recent breakthroughs in quantum technology, the idea of a globous and self-replicating mass of tiny robots, capable of stripping away the strongest steel, is edging from science fiction to science fact. Faced with such realities, many argue that International Humanitarian Law has a moral and legal responsibility to regulate new technologies.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_jmfsbs_of_war:
Greenfist
Ghosts of War

The human cost of war is cleverly executed in this clear but effective digital image. On close inspection, we can see that the ghostly silhouettes of the dead represent the losses of all sides and factions; spirits of fallen comrades appear to mingle with those of the enemy and all appear to be accompanying the grieving soldier in the mid-ground. The chiaroscuro effect is also ingeniously used, separating the living from the dead by way of light and shade.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_f16s_over_ktow:
Yooles
F-16s Over K-Town

Combat aircraft led to a revolution in the way that wars were waged, defining many conflicts over the last 100 years. But what will be the next seismic shift in warfare? What will be the 21st Century’s ‘Guernica’? A sky, dark with unmanned bombers? Clouds of miniature drones, subjugating nations at the touch of a button? Or will aerial engagements become a thing of the past, slowly superseded by battles in space?
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_ecce_homo:
Yooles
Ecce Homo

Behold the man. But a generation ago, how many would recognize this special forces operative as a man at all? There is no evidence of anything beneath the armor. Is this then, a sign of things to come? At what point, in a world of human enhancements and inchoate cybernetics, do we begin to lose ourselves? And what are the implications of dehumanizing combatants on the battlefield? How will this affect our perceptions of war? Is this another step in the sanitization of modern warfare? Or a simple practicality, providing soldiers with the equipment and protection needed?
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_dogs_of_peace:
Maria Komarova & Diana Pomortseva
Dogs of Peace
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_crossroads:
Victor Fievet
At the Crossroads of Two Worlds
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_concept_strike:
Maxi Cortés
Concept for Automated Strike Helicopter
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_concept_aa_veh:
Maxi Cortés
Concept for Automated AA Vehicle

A much neglected aspect of war art concerns the conceptualization of ideas. Although many of us would accept the 15th Century scribblings of Leonardo da Vinci's siege weapons and fighting vehicles as art, contemporary works draw more complex reactions. Could it be our appreciation of innovative designs is tempered by their destructive potential? Or are there qualities in paintings such as this, that transcend their immediate application?
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_collateral_dam:
João Victor Gonçalves Mariottini
Collateral Damage

In this playful yet provocative scene, a paramedic carries a wounded individual on a stretcher while a pair of Livonian soldiers look on. The laptop reads 'EMP', an acronym for ElectroMagnetic Pulse. EMP weapons destroy electronics and are sometimes used indiscriminately in cyberwarfare, breaking International Humanitarian Law by targeting civilian as well as military infrastructure.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_blue_party_pri:
Bamslam
Blue Party Prison Riot

Not all wars are fought upon the battlefield. This photograph depicts the famous 1989 'Blue Party Prison Riot' at Andrzejów Detention Center in Livonia, an episode which made international headlines and quickly captured the imagination of the world. Inmates, along with several guards, in solidarity with national actions against the Soviet regime and angry with deteriorating living conditions, staged several weeks of protests before finally taking full control of the facility.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_bad_harvest:
Mark Bailey
Bad Harvest

This interesting work underscores the terrifying potential of entomological warfare. Although insects have been used in conflict since ancient times, such methods were finally forbidden by International Humanitarian Law in 1972, under the Biological and Toxic Weapons Convention. Nevertheless, possessing the means to devastate an enemy's food supply or spread deadly pathogens through agents such as fleas or mosquitoes remains a tempting prospect for some.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_autonomous_ava:
Nicolas Humphrey
Autonomous Avarice

A harrowing representation of a civilian casualty, killed by a sniper drone. The victim's position in the foreground and the saturated palette used by the artist lends the scene a somber immediacy, reminding the viewer that a 'human in the loop' is not without risk and that questions regarding battlefield responsibility are unlikely to disappear any time in the near future, regardless of technological developments.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_a_childs_dream:
Aubrianna Rachmad
A Child's Dream

It's long been said that war brings out the worst and the best in us. As this heart-warming painting suggests, conflict can offer powerful opportunities for compassion. Indeed, it is in the wake of earth-shattering adversity that positive actions matter most.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_accident_near_:
Chace Smith
Accident Near Checkpoint

This unusual photograph was taken from the air and provides a unique perspective. On the road below, emergency services attempt to save the lives of civilians whose vehicle overturned after fleeing a military checkpoint. It was subsequently discovered that the driver missed warning signs and failed to reduce speed, finally panicking and crashing when warning shots were fired.
