str_a3_showcase_aow_infographic1:
Fully Autonomous Weapon Systems

Fully autonomous weapon systems (as opposed to partial autonomous weapon systems) are those that are capable of independently identifying, acquiring, and engaging targets, without human input. Since the late 2020s, such technology has been used worldwide, allowing nation states to conduct devastating offensive operations. Casualties are often one-sided and politically divisive.

(Text Box #1)

There is no clear consensus on what constitutes meaningful human control with fully autonomous systems. The relationship that exists between operators and robots is complex and constantly changing, leading to gaps and loopholes in legal frameworks. Laws, like technology, are in continuous flux.

(Text Box #2)

Despite advances in artificial intelligence and targeting algorithms, robots lack the ability to exercise human judgement and cannot make sense of important contextual information; without humans 'in the loop' it can be challenging to enforce International Humanitarian Law.

(Text Box #3)

Robots can separate individuals from their actions, frustrating attempts to assign legal and ethical responsibilities. Accountability is often difficult to determine; if something goes wrong, who is to blame? The manufacturer? The operator? The enemy? The officer in command? Or the robot itself?

(Text Box #4)

Mitigating the human cost of conflict in terms of soldiers' lives has far-reaching and serious implications. The fact that robots allow governments to wage war with impunity also makes the decision to go to war easier; effectively shifting the consequences of such actions into the civilian sphere.

(Statistics)

In 2035...

3505 people were killed in drone strikes...

1472 (42%) of these people were legitimate targets...

1857 (53%) of these people were civilians...

620 (33%) of these civilians were children...

These statistics are comparable to data collected in 2020, although with a commensurate increase, owing to a five-fold surge in operational usage.
str_a3_showcase_aow_infographic2:
Can robots support International Humanitarian Law?

Certainly! Although originally designed for military use, many types of robot have since been appropriated by humanitarian organizations and put to work clearing minefields, evacuating civilian casualties from combat zones, or delivering life-saving aid. Technological innovation provides a great many opportunities, which can affect positive change and build a better world.

(Text Box #1)

Removing landmines and Explosive Remnants of War (ERW) is a dangerous job, requiring highly skilled Explosive Ordnance Disposal experts. But with the help of re-purposed drones, risks are now being reduced and other hazards, such as lingering chemical and biological agents, can be detected.

(Text Box #2)

Getting supplies and medical aid to civilians in conflict zones puts aid workers in peril. However, with packbots and utility drones, impossible feats of logistics are being achieved. Robots are travelling far and wide, traversing deserts and mountains and battlefields, bringing essentials to those in need.

(Text Box #3)

Military-grade reconnaissance drones, with night vision and thermal optics, have been used in recent years for remote legal observation, deterring violations of International Humanitarian Law. In several cases, robots conducting digital surveillance have prevented war crimes from occurring.

(Text Box #4)

Beginning with leaflet drops in the 2020s, robots have fulfilled an important role in promoting landmine awareness and the Laws of Armed Conflict, providing interactive learning experiences for both soldiers and civilians, as well as disseminating basic emergency information.

Education
Risk Assessment
Protection and Shelter
Explosive Ordnance Disposal

str_a3_showcase_aow_label_czvd1:
Scarecrow
With thanks, together!

A Korean tourist took this picture of Czech soldiers and members of the "Civilisté děkují za službu" ("Civilians thank for service") group who participated in a local festival in the town of Bystrica. The Korean tourist who took this picture donated the photo to the "Civilisté děkují za službu" group.
str_a3_showcase_aow_label_czvd2:
refuse
Tribute to Czech Valor

Frozen in a tableau of quiet readiness, a phalanx of Czech soldiers stands as the custodians of history, positioned back-to-back in an unbreakable unity that symbolizes their interdependence – no era can exist without the other. Spread across the green tapestry of the homeland they pledged to protect, they bridge the chasms of time, each one embodying the indomitable spirit of the Czech military through the ages. From the antiquated patina of the Legionnaire’s rifle to the modern-day camouflage that whispers through the grasses, their uniforms narrate the story of their nation. Each soldier is a chapter, each weapon a verse in the epic of courage and sacrifice. The sky above, a brooding overture of clouds, seems to both salute and mourn the inexorable passage of time, while the earth beneath, speckled with the innocence of wildflowers, anchors the scene in the tranquility of the present. This is more than a mere assembly; it is a solemn tribute to Veterans Day, a canvas where the past breathes importance into the solemn promise of remembrance and honor.

str_a3_showcase_aow_stand_text_01:
Should we accept the human cost?

Robots may limit military casualties, but what does this mean for the future of modern conflict?

What is war without meaningful sacrifice? Are there ends that sometimes justify the means?

And if so, who decides?
str_a3_showcase_aow_stand_text_02:
Should humans still be in the loop?

It depends on who you ask. Some argue fully autonomous robots, capable of making split-second decisions, save lives.

Others insist that such robots cross a moral threshold when programmed to kill, because they cannot make human choices.

str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_aow_pard: So what do you get when buying the DLC and thereby donating to the ICRC? Play a new <t color='%1'>singleplayer showcase</t> that is centered around the retrieval of a priceless piece of stolen art. You escort an expert from the British Cultural Rescue Initiative through the aftermath of armed conflict, while dealing with various complications common in contemporary and future conflict. While you play this scenario, you will spot great new sandbox assets to use. A collection of <t color='%1'>formal suits</t> especially, can be used in a wide range of scenarios: from VIP protection to HVT ops. A special <t color='%1'>parade dress</t> variant with extra decorative elements was made for the major military factions, so units can stage their own parades and other formal events. Topping off this selection of new premium gear is a series of more <t color='%1'>civilian-oriented backpacks</t>, which again can be used for a myriad of situations. To preview these additions, everyone is invited to visit the fictional Lars Blanken Gallery in Amsterdam, where a lot of amazing community art is on display. Buy your tickets today and be sure to inspect the labels for bits of background trivia. And to repeat it once more: all of this premium content will become fully available to everyone after the fundraising period of approximately a year.
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_aow_parc: It's fair to say this DLC is not the biggest one we've ever released. However, there is an important element to keep in mind: all of our <t color='%1'>revenue from this DLC will be donated to the ICRC</t>. That means by purchasing it, you are contributing to their great worldwide work in conflict zones. As we've tried with the prior Laws of War DLC, we hope this release further spreads awareness of various important topics, such as IHL and the wartime protection of cultural property. After an initial fundraising period, the DLC will eventually become free to all owners of Arma 3.
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_aow_parb: Back in 2020, we hosted a <t color='%1'>'creators for charity' community contest</t>, which saw a diverse group of artists submit their work in various categories. After much deliberation, the jury then selected a line up of <t color='%1'>excellent winners</t>. They of course received their art-related prizes, gratitude, and community kudos. Our developers – led by Scott Alsworth – proceeded to take the contest results and enter a next phase of the project. As was always the plan, it was time now to build a <t color='%1'>charity DLC</t> around the same ethos. After evaluating the entries in the contest and our own ideas, we settled on several major themes. Obviously <t color='%1'>war</t> and <t color='%1'>art</t> were key, but still rather broad. We zoomed in on <t color='%1'>IHL in future conflict</t> (which itself was one contest category's theme) and <t color='%1'>military memorials</t> to bolster the DLC package. This led us to brainstorm about the format in which we wanted to showcase the community artwork and what other assets might fit that. The resulting content we hope is not only interesting as it is, but may lend itself for greater sandbox use in many scenarios. We would like to once again thank all contributors and winners for their efforts and for allowing us to showcase their work!
str_a3_rscdisplaywelcome_aow_para: We are humbled and honored to share with you this culmination of 2020's <t color='%1'>Art of War creator contest</t>. Driven by splendid community artwork submissions and further enriched by thematic pieces of content by us, this DLC is all about raising awareness and supporting a great real-world cause. Continuing our cooperation with the <t color='%1'>International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)</t>, we return to unique perspectives on war and International Humanitarian Law (IHL) especially. Welcome to the <t color='%1'>Art of War charity DLC</t>!

Russian military units remain active beyond the Kaliningrad border and biosecurity protocols mean access to the Visitation Site is restricted.

str_a3_c_intro1_article_neutrinos_textbo: Scientists worldwide confirm mysterious findings, indicating we are in the midst of a 'neutrino storm'.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_neutrinos_text9: "On average, 65 billion neutrinos move through every square centimetre of our planet, perpendicular to the sun – every second. Now we're seeing upwards of 200 billion. And it's consistent, across the globe.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_neutrinos_text8: "Most reach us from natural reactions occurring in the sun – but they also have artificial causes, like nuclear power stations or even nuclear weapons tests.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_neutrinos_text7: "They are created by radioactive decay," explained Dr. John Ogilvy, Lead Astronomer at the Cubic Kilometre Neutrino Telescope.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_neutrinos_text6: Neutrinos are small elementary particles that interact only with weak subatomic forces and gravity, making them difficult to detect.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_neutrinos_text5: "Whatever the cause, it's very exciting and could fundamentally change the way we think about our universe."
str_a3_c_intro1_article_neutrinos_text4: "It seems there really has been a three fold increase in the number of neutrinos passing through the Earth. It could be due to a huge supernova or blazar, or else, it might indicate the existence of neutrino clouds, or a yet unknown cosmic event.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_neutrinos_text3: "Our results were validated by both the IceCube Neutrino Observatory in Antarctica and the NEVOD Neutrino Detector in Moscow. It was only then that we realized, it wasn't a glitch in the system.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_neutrinos_text2: Project Manager, Negano Ishiguro, initially suspected a technical problem, saying "we did not think much of it, until the first calls came in from other observatories.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_neutrinos_text10: "That's the real mystery. The surge isn't coming from the sun, so we want to know where it's coming from. Our next task will be to compare data from different neutrino observatories in an attempt to localize the source."
str_a3_c_intro1_article_neutrinos_text1: The spike in neutrino detections started around 06:47 local time on Friday 10 June at the 'Super-K' Neutrino Observatory, located deep beneath Mount Ikeno, Japan.

str_a3_c_intro1_article_electron_textbol: US Forces arrive in Livonia for joint military exercises, amid growing concerns over Russia's CSAT status.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_electron_text9: But AAN's correspondent in Andrzejów, Sean Bradwell, says paranoia in Eastern Europe has reached a fever pitch since Belarus began accession talks with CSAT, following the 2035 Moscow Summit.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_electron_text8: Attending forces will focus on interoperability, CBRN (Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear) defenses, and Electronic Warfare.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_electron_text7: About 14,000 Livonian and 10,000 US personnel are taking part this week, as well as 1,000 from the UK and other NATO states.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_electron_text6: The Electron exercises began in 2035 and occur every two years.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_electron_text5: "A return to bilateral Cold War-era thinking could be disastrous for everyone. If the US continues to ignore the new world order, and insists on creating enemies where there are none, they run the risk of making their fears a reality."
str_a3_c_intro1_article_electron_text4: Foreign Minister Poda Makarovich said: "NATO sabre-rattling is counterproductive. The world is already on a precipice.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_electron_text3: Russia says that such a show of force, close to its borders, is a threat to its security.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_electron_text2: Named Excercise Electron-39, the event will be the biggest of its kind and comes just weeks ahead of a Kremlin decision on a CSAT membership action plan.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_electron_text11: Exercise Electron, Bradwell states, is a way of bolstering confidence at a time when CSAT looks poised to achieve complete global hegemony. If Russia enters the fold, it would mean the final and most important domino has fallen.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_electron_text10: He added that many in the West are still concerned over the 'Apex Protocol Papers' and the bloc's projection of soft power expansionism.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_electron_text1: Some 25,000 Livonian, US, and British troops are participating in joint training operations, less than 15 km from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad.
str_a3_c_intro1_article_electron_image2: The "Andrzejów Gap" is of great strategic importance, linking NATO Baltic States to the rest of Europe.

Message received, any idea how much it can take, sir? Over.
str_a3_c_outro2_002_mothership_departure: Copy. Expedite! The alien has disengaged. It already went inside.
Continue on task, the core is still vulnerable! Over.
Guess we gave the wrong impression.
It looks like they're leaving. Out.
str_a3_c_outro2_001_tactical_briefing_ca: Get on it, or everything is fucked!
Go! Protect core. Fall out of here.
Alien is giving Livonian forces hell. But danger is core. It is destructible, weak.
If it would be destroyed, all this?
Ash and ruin, or maybe, much worse.
You and I must be ready to lay down heads, American.
str_a3_c_outro2_001_tactical_briefing_pl: I know. I got it, we're expendable!
str_a3_c_outro2_001_tactical_briefing_ca: Our teams have tracker beacons active. You can see on your device.
Sergeant? Did you get a fix on him?
str_a3_c_outro2_001_tactical_briefing_op: He's close, Comrade Captain. On the hill, one from ours.
str_a3_c_outro2_001_tactical_briefing_ca: I must hold position, radio general in Kaliningrad.
str_a3_c_outro2_001_tactical_briefing_op: Follow my lead, we're not stopping!
str_a3_c_freeroam1_overviewtext: Efforts are made to regain control of a desperate situation.
str_a3_c_freeroam1_journal_russianleafle:
Warning!
You have been exposed to an unknown pathogen.
The Russian Federation must act now to enforce cross-border quarantine measures, in the interests of biological security.
Such actions are in accordance with Federal Constitutional Law N 3-FKZ (2021) and WHO International Health Regulations, Article XVI. AM II. (2024).
This is not an act of war nor an attempt to undermine the sovereignty of Livonia.
For your own safety, remain where you are and avoid human contact. Comply with law enforcement officials, medical workers, and military personnel.
str_a3_c_freeroam1_journal_rootresearch_:
There are limits to what we can achieve with the root cap in situ at the SIŁA Factory.

Clearly, it is part of a much larger structure. This is why I'm filing a formal request for the creation of a pilot hole - and yes, it will involve 'conspicuous' drilling equipment and contractors. Simply put, there's no way round it. The discovery is far too deep. If you want to establish linkage with the specimen on the hill, we must go deeper.

Dr. Lem, I know you're busy. I'm summarizing here.

Today's results on the infrared scan. The internal component of the root's internode, colloquially referred to as the 'tongue', gave a marked response to the thermal signatures provided. Dr. Čapek believes this could be an evolutionary trait. Personally, I am not convinced - at least, not until we conclude our preliminary tests.

Nevertheless, on each occasion when thermal signatures were applied in close proximity, the tongue retracted. If it is indeed organic, it will be utterly incongruous with the syntheticity observed elsewhere. Of course, we'll know more once the science bot and genome sequencing equipment arrives.

The sample we collected from the root in the field has biomineralized. There is nothing left but a crystalline matter, black in color.

This process has been triggered by an unknown factor. Possibly the injection of some kind of stimulant - maybe even extraterrestrial in origin?

I can only speculate on the purpose behind this transformation.
str_a3_c_freeroam1_journal_evacuationnot:
NOTICE OF MANDATORY EVACUATION

Toxic vapors have leaked from the former SIŁA Factory. This area is NOT safe!

In accordance with Ministry of Health legislation (Act on Mass Event Safety [2023]), you are required to leave the Nadbór region immediately.

* Open shelters are located at Radunin and Topolin.
* Listen to a battery-powered radio and follow local evacuation instructions.
* Collect Emergency Supply Kits from military personnel.
* Take your pets, but only service animals are permitted in public shelters.
* Follow the recommended evacuation routes. Do not take shortcuts. Alternative routes may be blocked.

Do not remain in the affected area. Doing so endangers your life and the lives of first responders.
str_a3_c_freeroam1_007_am_player_finds_r: Shit, we nearly opened up on you...
God, yeah, no! After that breakout?
Hell. I dunno how we can ever repay you. That's a life debt.
Pulling shit up out the ground - we saw them. Seriously, it was fucking insane, man.
Maybe we didn't disturb the roots?
That doctor at the camp - he reckoned they're here for those  roots. That they're here because we disturbed them somehow... that make sense to you?
Maybe, they did? They could've been on their way here for like, months?
I wonder how they got here so fast?
If you need any gear, take whatever you want.
Months. Or millions of years. Space is pretty fucking spacious, Cooper.
Come sunrise, we're all going AWOL.
str_a3_c_freeroam1_006_am_player_unties_: Sure, stay off the roads. And don't go back to Kresnik.
There's no one there, we're staying on the move.
str_a3_c_freeroam1_003_am_player_enters_: Hey, you guys wanna get outta here?
No, you go. I gotta fuck-ton of mad shit that I gotta do tonight...
Cut us loose - we'll bolt. I know a place we can all lay low.
str_a3_c_freeroam1_002_ex_player_leaves_: Screw this. I'm heading outta here.
str_a3_c_freeroam1_001_ex_player_leaves_: Shit. I really better check my map.
STR_A3_C_Diary_Briefing_desc: My personal notes on the situation...
STR_A3_C_Diary_FreeRoam1_desc:
First Contact...

Imagine the Indians of the New World greeted Columbus with arrows. That's about where we are now. Actually, no; our situation's worse. Imagine they did that, then fought on the beach with another tribe. My only hope is these aliens are as disinterested in us as they seem - but then, why are they here?

Lieutenant Kingsly wants us to gather intel, although that won't exactly be easy with all the LDF around. Suffice to say, we're none too popular after Corporal Stype's stunt with the explosives at Camp Kresnik. Seems it's true what they say: the road to hell really is littered with good intentions. I guess, whatever happens, it's going to be a long night.
STR_A3_C_Diary_Intro1_desc:
So much for Livonia's 'summer sunshine'. And I thought the Pacific was bad...

Anyway, seems I've been temporarily assigned to an Electronic Warfare team - we're operating in the thick of it, behind enemy lines. Somehow today is going to reflect that. We're supposed to be attacking an abandoned factory - they gave us tetanus shots and everything. I guess it means we'll see some 'action'...
STR_A3_C_Diary_Intro2_desc:
Looks like we're going home early. Or at least, that was the idea.

Watching AAN tonight, I'm not so sure we're going anywhere - the National Movement Control Points are completely rammed and all our travel permits need replacing. The Livonians? They're not exactly forward thinkers - you can't just 'move' an army. Cancelling Exercise Electron because of that business at the factory, I mean, talk about a kneejerk reaction. We don't even know what went wrong...
STR_A3_C_Diary_Intro3_desc:
No time to write and the glow from a chemlight's fading...

If Corporal Jack Stype and I disappear, know this: we saw an alien object in the sky. It passed right overhead. And there is something or some things, buried beneath the SIŁA Factory.

Soon enough, everyone will know - we're going to Camp Kresnik.
STR_A3_C_Diary_FreeRoam2_desc:
It seems we've got a new lead.

Our science team has jerry-rigged the Russian neutrino Bouncer on the mini UGV. If it does what we think it does, I should be able to follow the subterranean roots to their tips - which appear to be of interest to the aliens. If we can get just more samples, we might be able to learn if there's a danger from contamination.
STR_A3_C_Diary_Outro2_desc:
Apparently we share a common interest with the Russians.

I guess there's nothing like 'survival' to bring us all together. No doubt, they'll exploit this mess to their advantage but right now, we have no choice. If we can't stop the LDF's offensive, everything is lost.
str_a3_c_outro3_overviewtext: The world reflects on First Contact.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText38: The Siła Factory closed down and relocated in 1995, due to structural instability.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText39: Livonia's neighbor, Belarus, is in accession talks with CSAT, following the 2035 Moscow Summit.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText40: On July 15, 2039, Russia will consider an action plan for joining CSAT. Many Livonians fear that membership will end a tenuous balance of world power.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText41: Due to increasing tensions with Russia, a growing number of Livonians are joining civilian militias.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText42: In 1982, a group of triangular shaped UFOs were spotted over Livonia's Lukow Airfield.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText43: Crop circles are a common phenomenon in Livonia.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText44: The first widely reported UFO sighting in the USA was made by Kenneth Arnold in 1947, also spawning the term "flying saucer" in press reporting.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText45: Many believe an extraterrestrial spacecraft crash-landed near the town of Roswell, USA, in 1947. The government has always denied this.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText46: Following projects Sign and Grudge, project Blue Book was a US Air Force study into UFOs. It concluded there was no evidence of extraterrestrials and that these sightings were not a threat.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText47: The Wow! signal was a powerful deep space radio transmission that has never been adequately explained as having a terrestrial or natural source.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText48: The UK government declassified their Alsworth Report in June 2029, analyzing in great detail the possible implications of the discovery of extraterrestrial life.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText49: SETI is the search for extraterrestrial intelligence, often focused on potential alien transmissions in the electromagnetic spectrum.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText50: In 1974, the Arecibo message, containing info about Earth and humanity, was sent into space. Not everybody agrees with making our presence known in this way.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText51: The scientific study of extraterrestrial life is also referred to as xenology.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText52: High probability estimates for extraterrestrial life and the lack of evidence of such life are analyzed in the Fermi paradox.
STR_A3_C_CfgWorlds_Enoch_LoadingText53: 2026's multiple meteor impacts in Dongting Lake near Changsha, China, triggered worldwide conspiracy theories on extraterrestrial invasions.
STR_A3_C_CfgMods_Contact_overview: The Arma 3 Contact expansion is a military science fiction experience about humanity's first encounter with extraterrestrial intelligence on Earth. The alien motivations being unknown, you will use field science and combat reconnaissance to uncover their technologies and determine their intentions. Amid the tension and chaos, authentic armed conflict inevitably unfolds.
STR_A3_C_CfgMods_Contact_CB_Campaign_des: You are a member of a NATO deployment to a remote region of Livonia, presented with a mysterious event that will change the face of human history forever.
STR_A3_C_CfgMods_Contact_CB_ETMothership: Very little is yet known about the extraterrestrial visitors, but their largest known vessel is hard to miss. Presumably employing a form of gravity control, it appears to have little trouble maintaining levitation, even given its size. Various theories exist concerning the ET means of interstellar transportation. It is, however, not confirmed whether these large entities travel by themselves, by means of a yet bigger vessel potentially in orbit of our planet, or by an entirely different method.
STR_A3_C_CfgMods_Contact_CB_ETProbe_desc: This mysterious underground network stretches for many kilometers. Its purpose and origins are completely unknown, but it would appear to be incredibly old. Still, it has gone unnoticed by humanity for the longest time.
STR_A3_C_CfgMods_Contact_CB_ElectronicWa:
Control the electromagnetic spectrum to locate, study, deceive, and ultimately defeat your enemies.

Note: this feature is scripted and created for use in Contact's singleplayer campaign primarily.
STR_A3_C_CfgMods_Contact_CB_ETDrone_desc: Speculated to be the extraterrestrials' main surveyors of Earth, these car-sized entities utilize technology far beyond human understanding. Early sighting reports have mentioned orbiting functional modules, but much more research is needed before their true capabilities and purpose can be evaluated.
STR_A3_C_CfgMods_Contact_CB_FieldScience:
Use various tools, such as a mini UGV sampling laser and CBRN (Chemical Biological Radiological Nuclear) defense equipment, to study strange alien anomalies.

Note: these features as well as the extraterrestrial simulations are mostly scripted and created for use primarily in Contact's singleplayer campaign.
STR_A3_C_fnc_drawTooltip_dangerZone: A danger zone with increased enemy activity. Manual saving and time acceleration are not available while inside.
str_a3_c_fnc_showsimplenotification_dang: Manual saves and time acceleration are disabled.
Manual saves and time acceleration are available again.
str_a3_c_fnc_showsimplenotification_mini: Connection to %1 lost due to heavy damage.
str_a3_c_cfg3den_layer_contactcondition_: Condition for layer entities to be spawned when a whole site is spawned.
str_a3_c_cfg3den_group_bin_reinforcement:
When the group is no longer in "SAFE" mode, it will call for reinforcements only when this condition returns true.
Passed variables are:
 _this # 0 - group
 _this # 1 - time since the group became alert
str_a3_c_cfg3den_group_bin_enablerespons: When disabled, squad will not reply to any received signals. Use only when you replace it by your own response system.
str_a3_c_cfg3den_group_bin_deceptionmove: Group can be deceived, but returns back to the first patrol point after some time.
Group can be deceived and stays wherever player sends it.
Deception is an ability to issue orders to the squad (e.g. "Move West").
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_xrays_tooltiptex: X-rays pass through most objects, making them useful for generating images of tissue and structures inside the human body. They are also used in astronomy for observing stars and black holes.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_wifi1_tooltiptex: Today, the frequency of wireless Internet connects countless digital devices. Being at the higher end of the spectrum its range is limited, but it does allow larger bitrates.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_vlf_tooltiptext: Used for radio navigation or radio clocks, and was used for wireless telegraphy in early 20th century.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_vhf_tooltiptext: For this band, antennas can be small enough to be made man-portable. They are used for FM radio, television, military handhelds, and countless other communication devices.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_ultraviolet_tool: These are produced by black lights, tanning lamps, and also by our sun. Though they are mostly absorbed by Earth's atmosphere, prolonged exposure can still be harmful to people.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_ulf_tooltiptext: Ultra Low Frequencies can move through soil and are sometimes used for mining communications.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_uhf_tooltiptext: These are predominantly used for television broadcasting, cell phones, satellite communications (including GPS), Wi-Fi, and many other systems that need to transmit large amounts of data.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_tv1_tooltiptext: Here we have the band for television channels. Because video and sound need more data, every channel requires a wider frequency band, and the number of these is limited - leading to competition over unallocated bands.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_ti_tooltiptext: Thermal Imaging (TI), occasionally known as FLIR (Forward-Looking InfraRed), has a variety of military applications, especially in terms of recon and targeting.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_slf_tooltiptext: This frequency can penetrate seawater hundreds of meters deep, which is frequently put to use in submarine communications. However, it requires extremely large antennas to transmit and receive.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_shf_tooltiptext: Super High Frequencies are utilized by some types of radar and they are essential for microwave heating - including microwave ovens.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_radiowaves_toolt: As the name suggests, radio waves were first used for radios and later, television and military communications. They are widely used for transmitting information over long distances. Frequencies are strictly regulated by governments and international bodies.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_microwaves_toolt: Microwaves, like radio waves, are used mainly for communication. Their shorter wavelength allows for smaller antennas and a larger bitrate - but also require line of sight. They are the preferred medium for radars and remote sensing.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_mf_tooltiptext: Apart from the widely known AM radio, this band also includes maritime communications and distress beacons.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_lf_tooltiptext: Low Frequencies can travel considerable distances owing to their ability to diffract across terrain and travel beyond the horizon - a method known as 'ground wave' propagation. These are employed by radio navigation and meteorological information broadcasts.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_laser_tooltiptex: Lasers are highly amplified light beams in infrared and visible spectra. They are used for range calculations and targeting by the military, and by civilians for barcode scanning, surgery, cutting, welding, and exercising cats...
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_infrared_tooltip: Infrared radiation is known for transmitting heat and has many civil and military applications, ranging from thermal imaging, weather forecasting and spectroscopy to missile homing, tracking and night vision optics.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_ieee_l_tooltipte: This is an older NATO designation of a frequency band.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_hf_tooltiptext: High Frequencies propagate through 'skywave', where the signal is reflected from the ionosphere and can travel beyond the horizon. These are employed in aviation, military, and amateur radio communications.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_gammarays_toolti: In nature, gamma rays are created by radioactive decay and are extremely dangerous to humans.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_fm_tooltiptext: FM stands for 'Frequency Modulation', which means that sound is transmitted by the constant changing of a signal's frequency. A radio station operating on 88.2 MHz, for example, may in fact be using a band between 88.1 and 88.3 MHz.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_elf_tooltiptext: These are generated by lightning and disturbances in Earth's magnetic fields.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_ehf_tooltiptext: EHF is sometimes referred to as the millimeter band. It is used in radars, point-to-point communications, and airport security screening.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_cellphone1_toolt: This is the frequency dominated by mobile phones. Bands on lower frequencies allow companies to cover larger areas, while those on higher frequencies are useful for serving customers across smaller regions.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_visiblelight_too: Electromagnetic waves visible to the human eye, perceived as colors by our brain. This is everything we see around us.
str_a3_c_rscmapspectrum_am_tooltiptext: AM means 'Amplitude Modulation'. It conveys sound by changing a signal's strength, which makes it particularly vulnerable to static interference. Widespread during the 'Golden Age of Radio', its popularity waned as FM radio became more common.
STR_A3_C_RscDisplayMain_LogoContact_tool: View the Arma 3 Contact Welcome Screen again.

STR_A3_C_RscDisplayMain_Multiplayer_tool: Play multiplayer scenarios (note: scenarios that are not designed for Arma 3 Contact may not be compatible).

STR_A3_C_CfgHints_PremiumContact_desc: The Arma 3 Contact expansion is a military science fiction experience about humanity's first encounter with extraterrestrial intelligence on Earth. The alien motivations being unknown, you will use field science and combat reconnaissance to uncover their technologies and determine their intentions. Amid the tension and chaos, authentic armed conflict inevitably unfolds.%1%11%1%2"First Contact" - you are a member of a NATO deployment to a remote region of Livonia, presented with a mysterious event that will change the face of human history forever.%1%2Extraterrestrials - meet visitors from outer space, bringing their own technology, vessels, scientific instruments, and defensive measures%1%2Electronic Warfare - control the electromagnetic spectrum to locate, study, deceive, and ultimately defeat your enemies%1%2Field Science - use various tools, such as a mini UGV sampling laser and CBRN defense equipment, to study strange alien anomalies%1%2Spectrum Device - wield this advanced modern tool and its range of antennas for Electronic Deception, navigation, and intelligence gathering
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_BiopsySampling_arg0: It physically grabs a small sample of soft tissue or loose material, and stores it in an on-board secure container. These samples are later analyzed in a (field) laboratory.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_BiopsySampling_desc: Mounted on the <t %5>ED-1E mini UGV</t> variant is a telescopic <t %5>biopsy probe</t>. %14%1%2Switch to the UGV's optics view using %11 for aiming.%1%2Select the tool using %12.%1%2Position the UGV and its arm into a suitable and unobstructed position.%1%2Use %13 for the probe lance to take its sample.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Spectrum_tip: Waves in each band have different characteristics, interactions with matter, sources, and applications.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Spectrum_desc: The <t %5>electromagnetic spectrum</t> is the <t %5>range of frequencies</t> of <t %5>electromagnetic radiation</t> with their wavelengths and photon energies.%1%1Common <t %5>frequency bands</t>:%1%2<t %5>Radio waves</t>: communications, astronomical objects, etc.%1%2<t %5>Microwaves</t>: radar, cell phones, satellites, quick meals, etc.%1%2<t %5>Infrared</t>: thermal vision, targeting systems, etc.%1%2<t %5>Visible light</t>: anything we humans can see%1%2<t %5>Ultraviolet</t>: tanning lamps, black lights, etc.%1%2<t %5>X-rays</t>: radiology, etc.%1%2<t %5>Gamma rays</t>: nuclear decay, cosmic events, etc.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_ElectronicWarfare_tip: A range of frequencies of electromagnetic radiation make up the electromagnetic spectrum.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_ElectronicWarfare_desc: In <t %5>Electronic Warfare (EW)</t> the <t %5>electromagnetic spectrum</t> is controlled to attack or otherwise impede enemies. Similarly, utilization of this spectrum can be used for less offensive goals, such as <t %5>scientific field study</t> and <t %5>communications</t>.%1%2<t %5>Receiving</t>: locating, identifying, listening to, and recording signals%1%2<t %5>Transmitting</t>: jamming, sending data, radar detecting, and direct energy damaging%1%2<t %5>Blocking</t>: signal path distorting
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_BiopsySampling_tip: Biopsy samples require very precise aim. The lance also has a small range, so check the HUD to learn whether you are in range of any surface.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SignalStrength_desc: Various factors can influence <t %5>signal quality</t> in the electromagnetic spectrum (the 'link budget').%1%1<t %5>Receivers / Transmitters</t>:%1%2<t %5>Position</t>: higher places provide better 'line of sight' and fewer obstructions%1%2<t %5>Power</t>: stronger signals are easier to receive%1%2<t %5>Antenna</t>: frequencies affect data and quality, gain controls effectiveness, and direction can matter too%1%1<t %5>Path</t>:%1%2<t %5>Distance</t>: signal strength deteriorates with range%1%2<t %5>Environment</t>: obstructions like hills and vegetation can weaken signals%1%2<t %5>Weather</t>: rain can weaken signal strength at higher frequencies (hard to observe)
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SignalStrength_tip: Lost track of a signal? Try to reach an elevated position without object obstruction.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SpectrumDevice_tip: Pick the right antenna for the job! You will not receive all signals on a single antenna.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SpectrumDevice_desc: The <t %5>Spectrum Device</t> uses the <t %5>sidearm slot</t>. It allows for the <t %5>reception</t> and <t %5>transmission</t> of electromagnetic <t %5>signals</t>. There are several functional components:%1%2<t %5>Grip</t>: the main shared body (%11 to select).%1%2<t %5>Screen</t>: switch analyzer detail modes (%12 to switch)%1%2<t %5>Antennas</t>: attach to operate within different frequency ranges (%13 to swap).%1%2<t %5>Flashlight</t>: use the device in the dark (%14 to toggle).
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SignalStrength_desc_hi: Various factors can influence <t %5>signal quality</t> in the electromagnetic spectrum (the 'link budget').%1%2<t %5>Receivers / Transmitters</t>: position (elevated, good 'line of sight', no obstructions), power, antenna (frequency range, gain, direction)%1%2<t %5>Path</t>: distance, environment (obstructions like hills and vegetation)
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_CBRN_desc: <t %5>C</t>hemical, <t %5>B</t>iological, <t %5>R</t>adiological, and <t %5>N</t>uclear defense is protective measures in situations where such hazards may be present. Specifically biochemical threats may be encountered and prove damaging without protection.%1%1<t %5>P</t>ersonal <t %5>P</t>rotective <t %5>E</t>quipment (PPE), such as <t %5>A</t>ir <t %5>P</t>urifying <t %5>R</t>espirators (APR) and over-garments can provide limited protection. Especially for military personnel there is a balance between protection and tactical effectiveness. Reduced maneuverability and fatigue are common PPE burdens.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_CBRN_tip: Without proper decontamination, treating symptoms may not be enough.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_ChemicalDetector_desc: Some hazards may be observed visibly, but others require specialized detectors to detect. The <t %5>chemical detector</t> samples air constantly and will sound an <t %5>audible warning</t> when a threat is detected.%1%2Hold or double-tap %11 to bring up an equipped detector.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_ChemicalDetector_tip: The audio alarm will sound even without looking at the detector.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_DangerZones_desc: Several missions in Contact divide the Area of Operations in so-called '<t %5>danger zones</t>'.%1%1Within these zones <t %5>special rules apply</t>:%1%2Manual saves are not available.%1%2Time acceleration is not available.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SDEquipping_tip: You cannot have an actual sidearm equipped at the same time, so use your primary weapon for defense instead.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Transmitting_tip: Jamming is simply sending a signal at a frequency which you want to deny someone from using effectively.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Transmitting_desc: An equipped <t %5>Spectrum Device</t> can <t %5>transmit signals</t> on the <t %5>selected frequency band</t> (e.g. noise or a message).%1%2Use %11 and %12 to select the frequency band.%1%2Aim the transceiver directly at an antenna for successful reception.%1%2<t %5>Hold</t> %13 to fully send the selected signal.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SDEquipping_desc: Equip the <t %5>Spectrum Device</t> like a <t %5>sidearm</t>.%1%15%1%2Use the %14 action to directly pick it up, or drag it into the desired slot via the inventory menu %11.%16%1%2You don't need to manage depletable resources like batteries.%1%2Use %12 to directly switch to the equipped device.%1%2Use %13 to switch between it and a primary weapon.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_DangerZones_tip: Your progress is saved upon entering a danger zone. Be on your guard while inside!
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_DroneHacking_desc: In some cases it may be possible to spoof <t %5>drone</t> access and <t %5>alter its routines</t>. Some of these routines may prove dangerous!%1%2Jam the drone by transmitting noise at its frequency (%14 MHz) using the Spectrum Device (Experimental antenna).%1%2Carefully get <t %5>close enough</t> for the drone to be able to receive your spoofing signal.%1%2<t %5>Hold</t> %11 and select the %13 signal.%1%2Precisely aim the device at the drone antenna.%1%2<t %5>Hold</t> %12 until the signal is fully sent.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SDDisplay_tip: The Jammer Antenna has a fixed frequency and detailed mode is not available with it attached.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SDDisplay_desc: On the <t %5>Spectrum Device</t> grip there is a small <t %5>multi-function display</t> with integrated <t %5>spectrum analyzer</t>. You see the basic mode by default, but can switch to detailed mode using %11.%1%2<t %5>Basic</t>: selected frequency band, signal strength, reception or transmission status, and compass%1%2<t %5>Detailed</t>: full antenna bandwidth, selected frequency band, signal strengths, selected transmission signal, reception / transmission status, and compass (with active task %12 / custom waypoint %13 / HQ %14 indicators)
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_DroneHacking_tip: A successful hack will switch off the drone's lights, while blinking lights indicate you are not yet within range to spoof.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_DroneInterference_desc: There are several methods of <t %5>interfering</t> with autonomous <t %5>drones</t>.%1%2<t %5>Jamming</t>: use a Spectrum Device with appropriate antenna attached to send a strong signal on its frequency band. This forces it into default behavior, such as landing or stopping movement and weapons fire.%1%2<t %5>Hacking</t>: at a very close range, use a special Spectrum Device signal to spoof access and mess with its routines (caution - may prove dangerous).%1%2<t %5>Disabling</t>: physically approach a drone, and use a hold action to permanently disable it.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SDAntennas_tip: The device stores several properties, such as the selected transmission signal and frequency band, per antenna.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SDAntennas_desc: The <t %5>Spectrum Device</t> can be mounted with <t %5>different directional antennas</t>. These can receive / transmit signals on <t %5>varying frequency ranges (bandwidths)</t>. To <t %5>swap</t> antennas, use %11%15.%1%%12 <t %5>Military Antenna</t>: used for manipulation of military communications.%1%%13 <t %5>Experimental Antenna</t>: used for unconventional interactions, as well as for jamming some drones.%1%%14 <t %5>Jammer Antenna</t>: used only for drone interference.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Selecting_tip: The selected signal is shown on the device's display. This selection is stored per attached antenna.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Selecting_desc: By default your <t %5>Spectrum Device</t> will transmit indistinct digital noise, but you can also <t %5>select and transmit</t> special-purpose <t %5>signals</t>.%1%2With the device in your hands, <t %5>hold</t> %11 to show the selection menu.%1%2Select the signal category of your choice (%12, %13, or %14).%1%2Select the desired signal.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_DroneInterference_tip: Jamming is not permanent; its effects last for as long as you transmit or a little while longer.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SpectrumMap_tip: By clicking on an antenna's %15 icon in a frequency's tooltip, you can locate it on the topographic map.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SpectrumMap_desc: A special <t %5>spectrum map</t> is available to provide a different 2D view on the <t %5>broad electromagnetic spectrum</t>. It shows major frequency bands and common types of usage, as well as <t %5>frequencies and antennas</t> you have discovered.%1%2Use %11 to open the topographic map.%1%2Switch to the spectrum map using the toggle on the right of the screen %14.%1%2Control zoom using %12 and %13.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_EDHandshakes_desc: After learning a squad's callsign, you need to perform a '<t %5>handshake</t>' for further deception.%1%2With the Spectrum Device equipped, <t %5>hold</t> %11 to open the signal selection menu.%1%2Select either the %13 or %14 category, depending on who you wish to impersonate.%1%2Select the correct handshake signal, based on the callsign you will spoof.%1%2Transmit the handshake by aiming at the target and <t %5>holding</t> %12 until the signal has fully played.%1%2You will receive a positive response from the target if the deception was successful.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Receiving_tip: Many factors can affect signal quality, including hills and trees.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Receiving_desc: Equipping the <t %5>Spectrum Device</t> will <t %5>automatically receive signals</t> within its antenna's capabilities. It will <t %5>play</t> an audio interpretation of any <t %5>signal</t> on the <t %5>selected frequency band</t>.%1%2Use %11 to view the device's detailed display mode.%1%2Use %12 and %13 to select the frequency band.%1%2Or use %14 and %15 to jump between active signals.%1%2Aim the device directly at a signal source for the best quality.%1%2Keep focus for a while to scan, identify, and tag a signal.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_EDHandshakes_tip: Make sure the party you are impersonating do not hear your signals, or they may impose radio silence, preventing further deception!
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_EDOrders_arg0: %1%2It's possible to request reinforcements, but consider the consequences.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_EDOrders_desc: Having successfully performed a <t %5>handshake</t> with a <t %5>callsign</t> (such as a squad), you can now try to send <t %5>fake orders</t>.%1%2<t %5>Hold</t> %11 to open the Spectrum Device's signal selection menu, and select the order of choice.%1%2Move orders will send a squad in a certain direction. They may not comply when a squad is in combat or is ordered out of their AO.%1%2%14 will reveal a squad's exact and real-time map position for a while.%13%1%2Aim at the callsign target and transmit the order by <t %5>holding</t> %12 (fully send it!).
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_EDOrders_tip: Squads will typically return to their original behavior after a while, or if their radio operator finds out they have been deceived.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_EDPings_desc: <t %5>Squads</t> in the field will automatically send out <t %5>pings</t> at intervals or when <t %5>requested</t>. Ping signals can be scanned to identify <t %5>callsigns</t> (from the meta data) and positions.%1%2Point the Spectrum Device with Military Antenna in the direction of a possible squad.%1%2Select the squad's suspected frequency band using %11 and %12.%1%2Scan, identify, and tag the squad's auto-ping.%1%2Or select the %15 signal by <t %5>holding</t> %13 and picking it in the %16 category.%1%2Transmit the request by keeping aim on the squad and <t %5>holding</t> %14.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_EDPings_tip: Try to identify the person carrying a radio pack in a squad; they are your best target. You may also overhear a callsign during comms.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_ElectronicDeception_de: Certain factions have had to switch to older radio comms, so you can use the <t %5>Spectrum Device</t> with <t %5>Military Antenna</t> to <t %5>deceive</t> them. <t %5>Electronic Deception (ED)</t> is achieved by impersonating callsigns and transmitting fake orders.%1%2This works on patrolling <t %5>squads</t> and <t %5>HQ</t> (marked %11 on the device's compass).%1%2Successful deception requires awareness of the <t %5>correct callsigns</t>, or it may lead to HQ-imposed radio silence.%1%2It's also important to consider the <t %5>location and direction</t> of involved parties.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_ElectronicDeception_ti: If you want to impersonate HQ, make sure a target squad is not placed between yourself and said HQ. They would both receive your signals and become alerted to your ruse.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Jamming_tip: Jamming prevents a drone from receiving new instructions, typically placing it into an autonomous default behavior mode.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Passive_tip: When signal activity is detected, consider using your Spectrum Device for further study. You may uncover useful intelligence!
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Passive_desc: Carried with you at all times is an <t %5>omnidirectional antenna</t> that <t %5>passively and automatically monitors</t> a broad range of the electromagnetic spectrum for <t %5>signals</t>.%1%1You will be <t %5>notified</t> when there is newly discovered signal activity on any detectable frequency. If the signal was previously scanned, its identifier is shown.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Jamming_desc: A <t %5>Spectrum Device</t> with <t %5>Jammer Antenna</t> can only receive signals and transmit noise on a <t %5>fixed frequency</t>. It's used to detect or interfere with autonomous drones.%1%2Aim the device directly at a drone antenna for the best quality.%1%2Keep focus for a while to scan and tag its signal.%1%2<t %5>Hold</t> %11 to send interfering noise.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_ETComms1_desc: Several attempts at <t %5>first contact</t> with the <t %5>extraterrestrial visitors</t> have been attempted. Sound and visible light did not seem effective, but <t %5>microwave transmissions</t> prompt a response.%1%1Some observations:%1%2ET does not appear to want us close by, yet we need to get <t %5>within range</t> for a good signal.%1%2ET is broadcasting multiple signals. We may try to <t %5>transmit</t> on the same frequencies. There could be a <t %5>pattern</t>.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_ETComms1_tip: Our science staff has narrowed down the main frequency range ET is active on, and built an Experimental Antenna for the Spectrum Device to cover this bandwidth.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_ETComms2_arg0: %1%2Whether on purpose or not, ET is reacting also with light and even some sounds.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_ETComms2_desc: Based on prior attempts at <t %5>communications</t> with <t %5>ET</t>, some more observations were made.%1%2For effective transmissions, we need to <t %5>position</t> ourselves <t %5>inside the anomaly zone</t>.%1%2Pushing too close to the ET entity seems to trigger a less friendly response.%1%2There is a main strong 'tracking' signal, but it does not appear related to comms.%1%2<t %5>Secondary data signals</t> get transmitted in a certain order; our best guess is to <t %5>transmit anything</t> on the <t %5>same frequencies</t> in response. In other cases we may discover a <t %5>pattern</t> in the signal strengths or sequential order.%11
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Intel_tip: Via an antenna's icon tooltip, you open the special spectrum map for another view on the electromagnetic spectrum.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Intel_desc: Information about <t %5>discovered antennas</t> is noted down on your <t %5>map</t> %11.%1%2<t %5>Precision</t>: a scanned antenna is indicated by an area whose precision depends on signal distance.%1%2<t %5>Triangulation</t>: take multiple scans of an antenna, from different directions and closer ranges, to pinpoint a signal's exact origin %12.%1%2<t %5>Identification</t>: fully scanned antennas may show an identifying label.%1%2<t %5>Decay</t>: antennas scanned some time ago are more faded; this data may no longer be accurate!
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_ETComms2_tip: Our hope is to place the entity in a state that will let us approach it safely. Is this communication?
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_LaserSampling_arg0: It can rapidly identify most known elemental compositions from an extensive on-board library.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_LaserSampling_desc: The <t %5>ED-1E mini UGV</t> variant features a <t %5>sampling laser</t>. %14%1%2Switch to the UGV's optics view using %11 for aiming.%1%2Select the tool using %12.%1%2Position the UGV and its arm into a suitable and unobstructed position.%1%2<t %5>Hold</t> %13 until a full sample sequence has completed. Do not move the instrument during this step!
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_LaserSampling_tip: You can sample remotely, but your range is limited to just a few meters. The HUD will inform you of successful / failed results.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_MiniUGV_arg0: It's the preferred option for first encounters with anomalies thanks to its suite of sensors and instruments.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_MiniUGV_arg1: You don't need to interact with a terminal.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_MiniUGVArm_arg0: Depending on the variant, the arm's head comes equipped also with a sampling laser, biopsy probe and chemical detector, or a disruptor weapon and mine detector.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_MiniUGVArm_arg1: %1%2You can also perform a limited degree of analogue rotation of the arm's head.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_MiniUGVArm_desc: The ED-1 <t %5>mini UGV</t> has a <t %5>flexible arm</t> and a suite of <t %5>special cameras</t> (front/rear-facing drive and arm). %18%1%2Use %11 and %12 to cycle cameras.%1%2Use %13 to toggle available vision modes.%1%2Use %14 and %15 to move the arm vertically.%1%2Use %16 and %17 to move the arm horizontally.%19
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Tasks_tip: The Spectrum Device's display has a horizontal compass that will point out the active task %15.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Tasks_desc: <t %5>Tasks</t> in Contact work slightly differently than the Arma 3 main game. Primarily they are not visualized in the 3D world.%1%2Use %11 to quickly remind yourself of the active task.%1%2Use %12 to bring up the full task listing. Click the task title to assign another available task.%1%2View the topographic map using %13 to look for any known task locations. You can also open the task listing here.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_MiniUGVArm_tip: Skilled operators may flip a stuck UGV using its arm.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_MiniUGV_desc: The ED-1D <t %5>mini UGV</t> is used for various field science tasks during your mission. %11%1%2Use the <t %5>Disassemble</t> action to pack it into a backpack, and the <t %5>Assemble</t> action to deploy it onto the ground for use.%1%2<t %5>Connections</t> to the UGV are <t %5>automatically established</t>. %12%1%2When assembled, use the action menu to <t %5>take remote control</t> of the UGV.%1%2When damaged, you may need to approach the UGV and use a hold action to <t %5>repair</t> it.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_TasksAreas_tip: Task areas are also visualized as such on your topographic map; its center icon is not necessarily your objective!
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_TasksAreas_desc: Some <t %5>tasks</t> do not point to a specific position, but rather indicate an <t %5>area</t> (like a search zone).%1%2While <t %5>outside</t> the area, you are pointed towards it (e.g. on your Spectrum Device's compass %11).%1%2Once <t %5>inside</t> the area, the task indication changes %12, and you will need to <t %5>search</t> for the task's objective.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_MiniUGVMove_desc: The <t %5>mini UGV</t> can <t %5>move</t> over a multitude of terrain types, but take care or it may get flipped.%1%2Turn left and right using %11 and %12.%1%2Move forwards and backwards using %13 and %14.%1%2Speed up using %15.%1%2Enable special driving lights using the action menu, or the main arm light using %16.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_MiniUGVMove_tip: Mind the position of the arm, as it may affect the UGV's balance. Stow it for longer travel.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_MiniUGV_tip: Don't forget your UGV, you will need it! Check the map for its position when deployed.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Patrols_desc: There may be some chaos in the <t %5>%11</t>'s ranks after recent events, but they still do <t %5>patrol</t> the region. Fortunately the EMP has forced them to switch to an older form of radio comms, exploitable by us.%1%2Patrols may react to certain <t %5>distractions</t> and <t %5>Electronic Deception</t>.%1%2Use pings and position requests to <t %5>track patrols</t> using your <t %5>Spectrum Device</t> with Military Antenna.%1%2But if patrols sense trouble, they can call in <t %5>reinforcements</t>!
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_Patrols_tip: It may be wiser to avoid patrols in many circumstances!
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_ProbeMapping_desc: As of yet its workings are unknown, but the mysterious <t %5>measurement device</t> that was found appears to let us <t %5>map the underground alien structure</t>. It's been <t %5>mounted to the mini UGV</t> for power, and will <t %5>take readings on an interval</t>.%1%2Simply carry or drive the UGV anywhere you wish to map the underground network.%1%2Use %11 to open to topographic map.%1%2Switch to the special map using the toggle on the right of the screen %12.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_ProbeMapping_tip: Colors indicate range to a positive measurement (red is close). Where nothing was detected, the map stays empty.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SDAntennas_desc_hint: To quickly <t %5>swap</t> antennas, use %11 while the Spectrum Device is equipped.
STR_A3_C_CfgHints_SDEquipping_arg0: %1%2Drag and drop device attachments (e.g. antennas) into their slot or storage as you wish.
